QUESTION: Given a set of observed symptoms, can a system pick the smallest set of underlying causes that accounts for all of them, and how small can that explanation get before it stops covering everything?
MECHANISM: Parsimonious covering theory sets up a two-layer causal network. One layer is disorders, the other is manifestations, and a stored relation says which manifestations each disorder can produce. A case presents a set of observed manifestations. The solver then searches the powerset of disorders for subsets whose combined manifestation sets cover every observation, and among those covers it prefers the ones of minimum cardinality or the ones that are irredundant, meaning no member can be dropped without losing coverage. The output is a cover, or a set of competing covers, plus its size.
CANDIDATE: A candidate explanation, which is a subset of the disorder set. What varies is which disorders are in the subset and how many there are. What is judged is whether the subset covers all observed manifestations and how large the subset is.
WORLD: A fixed bipartite causal network. The world supplies the disorder inventory, the manifestation inventory, the causal edges between them at some density, and one presenting case, that is one particular manifestation set to be explained.
WHAT_CHANGES: The number of manifestations presented, the size of the hypothesis space of disorders, and the causal density of the network, which controls how many disorders can explain any given symptom and therefore how ambiguous the case is. Both integer axes arrived null and must be set by the operator.
MEASURED: The cardinality of the returned cover, an integer bounded below by 1 and above by the hypothesis space size, plus a boolean saying whether the cover is complete. On the bench only one of those two can be adjudicated.
INFORMATIVE_FAILURE: Rich. A failure to find any complete cover is a direct statement about the causal network, namely that at least one presented manifestation has no cause in the hypothesis space, which localises the defect to a specific symptom. A failure to reach the target parsimony while still covering everything yields the achieved size, which is an upper bound on the true minimum and is reusable as the preregistered threshold for the next run. Failures here are bounds, not noise.
SOURCE_CHECK: VERIFIED. Reggia, Nau and Wang, Diagnostic expert systems based on a set covering model, International Journal of Man-Machine Studies 19, 1983, pages 437 to 460, confirmed by search; the set covering model of diagnosis and the notion of parsimonious covers are correctly attributed.
BLOCKER: R-BACKEND needs a measurement channel, since no existing result field can carry a cover or its cardinality, and the payload cannot carry a causal network, so an adapter must both feed the network in and pull cover_size out; R-EXECUTOR is the same missing measurement, plus the fact that generating the network from one integer seed is a modelling choice nobody has made yet; R-COMPOSE is blocked on adjudication, because the interesting statement is a comparison of achieved size against a chance baseline, and the outcome rule is a single scalar comparison that cannot aggregate across specs.
FAITHFUL: A faithful implementation needs a generator that turns one integer seed into a bipartite causal network at a declared density, a declared presenting case drawn from that network, and a solver that returns a minimum-cardinality or irredundant cover. The result must expose at least cover_size and covered_all so the sealed outcome rule has a scalar to compare. Off-the-shelf set cover solvers and ILP packages already do the search, so the bench only has to build the instance, call out, and fossilize.
REDUCTION: A real one exists, and it is a null rather than a method. Represent a candidate explanation as a bitstring over the hypothesis space, one bit per disorder, and set length equal to the hypothesis space size. Fix bits to a candidate with exactly k ones and run repeats under sha256_index, so every repeat scores that fixed k-sparse explanation against an independently drawn hidden target set. Because the scorer is bit-match fraction, the score distribution for a k-sparse candidate against a uniform target is exactly computable, so a sweep over k at fixed length gives the chance baseline for how well an explanation of a given parsimony matches an unknown truth. NEW DESIGN CHOICE, since the axes are null: hypothesis space size 32, manifestation count 8, k swept over 1, 2, 4, 8, 16. WHAT IT PRESERVES: the fixed candidate judged against a hidden ground truth, the parsimony axis as an explicit independent variable, and the reproducible case identity carried by the seed. WHAT IT LOSES: the covering relation itself, and with it everything that makes this abduction. There are no manifestations, no causal edges, no coverage constraint, and no tradeoff between parsimony and completeness, so the score is set similarity and not explanatory adequacy. WHICH CLAIM IT SUPPORTS: only the eligibility claim, that an explanation of size k over a space of size L reaches similarity s to an unknown truth with probability p by chance. That is the denominator any later abduction result has to beat, and computing it first prevents freezing a parsimony threshold that chance alone would clear.

QUESTION: Which combination of dopant concentration and annealing time gives a thin film the highest charge-carrier mobility, and can a machine find it by choosing its own next experiment rather than following a human's plan?
MECHANISM: A robot runs a closed loop. Each iteration mixes an ink from a hole-transport material, a dopant and an additive at a chosen ratio; spin coats it onto a substrate; anneals it on a hotplate for a chosen time; photographs the film; takes an optical spectrum; and measures a current-voltage curve. A pseudomobility is computed from the conductivity and the film thickness. A model-based optimiser fits a surrogate to every measurement made so far and picks the next ratio and time. The loop repeats until the budget of physical experiments is spent.
CANDIDATE: A processing recipe, that is, one point in a two-dimensional continuous space of dopant ratio and annealing time. It is judged by the measured pseudomobility of the film it produces.
WORLD: A physical laboratory. It supplies the chemistry, the spin coater, the hotplate, the camera, the spectrometer and the probe station, and it also supplies the noise floor of each of those instruments. The response surface is unknown in advance and is only ever sampled, never revealed.
WHAT_CHANGES: The two recipe parameters from iteration to iteration, and, underneath that, genuine run-to-run physical variation between nominally identical recipes.
MEASURED: Pseudomobility, a positive continuous quantity, one value per film, plus the count of physical experiments consumed, an integer.
INFORMATIVE_FAILURE: A failed campaign still leaves the sampled response surface, which is the expensive part. Even with no recipe over threshold you keep every measured point, the instrument repeatability at replicated points, and the location of the best region reached. The most useful failure is a campaign where replicates disagree by more than the surface varies across the whole region: that says the measurement, not the chemistry, is the bottleneck, and it hands you the number that says so.
SOURCE_CHECK: VERIFIED. MacLeod et al., Science Advances 6, eaaz8867 (2020), the Ada self-driving laboratory, maximised hole mobility of organic hole transport materials by iterating ink mixing, spin coating, thermal annealing for variable time, imaging, spectroscopy and current-voltage measurement. Dopant ratio and annealing time are the paper's own axes and pseudomobility is its own reported quantity.
BLOCKER: R-BACKEND is missing an execution-backend capability, namely an adapter that hands a recipe to an instrument stack or a physics simulator and records its reading as a spec result, together with a provenance record, because a physical reading is not reproducible from seed_root and the fossil must record the observation rather than a recipe for recomputing it; R-COMPOSE is missing an adjudication capability, because the campaign-level question, did the optimiser cross threshold in fewer experiments than random sampling, compares two campaigns while the outcome rule is one field, one operator, one value; R-EXECUTOR is missing a measurement capability, because no existing payload can even express a pair of real-valued parameters, let alone return a continuous response.
FAITHFUL: A faithful version needs an external backend the engine calls, either a real instrument stack or a physics-based film model, and a provenance record binding each reading to the recipe, the instrument state and the operator. The bench would keep the loop, the budget and the fossil, and would have to accept results that are recorded rather than recomputable. Nothing about the sealed-spec architecture is wrong for this method; only the backend is absent, which is why this is cheap rather than deep.
REDUCTION: Encode a recipe as a single bitstring of length 16, eight bits of dopant ratio and eight bits of annealing time, in GRAY CODE (NEW DESIGN CHOICE). The Gray code is load-bearing rather than decorative: bench score is the fraction of matching positions, so Hamming-adjacent words are score-adjacent, and plain binary would place 0111 and 1000 far apart in the quantity the proposer sees while they are adjacent in the parameter they mean. Fix one world seed so every iteration faces one landscape, and run a producer-side closed loop of 24 single-repeat specs (NEW DESIGN CHOICE), proposing a word, reading the score, proposing the next. Pre-register the threshold at score at least 0.8125, which is 13 of 16, so it lies on the attainable 1/16 grid rather than between two reachable values. WHAT IT PRESERVES: the closed loop itself, a hard experiment budget, one hidden response surface learnable only by sampling, and per-experiment fossilisation of the exact recipe and the exact reading. WHAT IT LOSES: all physics; all instrument noise, because the bench score is bit-deterministic, so replicates are exactly equal and the single most important real failure mode, irreproducible measurement, cannot occur at all; and the surrogate's real advantage, because the hidden target is a single-peaked additive landscape rather than a materials response surface. WHICH CLAIM: only that the orchestration is sound, that is, that a budgeted closed loop can be driven, fossilised and adjudicated end to end and that a proposer reaches a pre-registered attainable threshold within budget. Because the landscape is unimodal and noiseless this doubles as a CEILING check: a proposer that fails here is broken. It licenses nothing whatever about materials and must not be reported as an optimisation result.

QUESTION: If you delete one gene from a yeast strain and then add one nutrient back into its food, does the yeast grow again? The answer is meant to hint at what the deleted gene was doing.
MECHANISM: Take a yeast strain in which exactly one open reading frame has been deleted. Grow it in a chemically defined medium that lacks the nutrient of interest, and in parallel in the same medium with that one nutrient added back. Incubate, and read optical density of the culture over time as the growth readout. A strain that fails to grow without the supplement and grows with it is auxotrophic for that nutrient, which places the deleted gene somewhere upstream in the pathway that makes it. In the real Robot Scientist loop this assay is not the whole method: a logical model of the metabolic pathway proposes which gene-enzyme pairing would predict which growth outcome, the machine picks the assay that best discriminates among live hypotheses, the robot physically runs it, and the outcome kills the hypotheses it contradicts. The growth assay is the single measurement at the bottom of that loop.
CANDIDATE: The knocked-out strain. What varies is which single gene is absent and which single nutrient is present.
WORLD: A defined liquid growth medium in a plate well at a set temperature. The environment supplies energy, every nutrient except the ones being withheld, and time. Crucially it supplies the SELECTIVE CONTEXT: the deletion is only visible because the medium refuses to give the cell what the missing gene would have made.
WHAT_CHANGES: Across runs, the identity of the deleted ORF and the identity of the added supplement. Everything else is held fixed by design, which is the whole point of a defined medium.
MEASURED: Final or maximum optical density, a continuous positive real, in practice compared against a no-growth control. Richer versions read the whole growth curve and extract lag time and doubling rate.
INFORMATIVE_FAILURE: Very informative. A knockout that grows anyway when you expected auxotrophy is the single most useful outcome in this method: it says a redundant or alternative route to the nutrient exists, which is a positive structural claim about the pathway. A knockout that fails to grow even WITH the supplement says the gene does something other than, or in addition to, making that nutrient. Both failures narrow the pathway. This is a method whose failures are its product.
SOURCE_CHECK: VERIFIED - King et al. 2009, The Automation of Science, Science, is real and describes exactly this: yeast deletion mutants, auxotrophic growth experiments, and hypothesis generation over orphan enzymes in the aromatic amino acid biosynthesis pathway. Caveat worth recording: the three ORFs named in param_space are not aromatic amino acid pathway genes as far as I can establish, and the listed supplements uracil, histidine and leucine are the standard laboratory auxotrophic MARKER nutrients rather than Adam's aromatic targets, so the parameter values look like generic yeast-genetics furniture rather than values drawn from the cited work. The method and the attribution are right; the numbers were not checked against the paper by whoever mined this.
BLOCKER: R-COMPOSE - the scientific content is an INTERACTION between two factors, does the supplement help more when the gene is missing, and the outcome rule is one field, one operator, one value, so the interaction cannot be adjudicated inside a spec. This is an ADJUDICATION blocker and it is the only one on this route, since the four cells can each be their own spec. R-BACKEND - no metabolic simulator is wired in; this is a MISSING MEASUREMENT rather than a substrate limit, because an external flux-balance model takes a gene deletion and a medium and returns a growth rate with no bench internals changed. R-EXECUTOR - if the reduced bitstring version below is wanted with the masking done inside the executor rather than by the producer, evaluate_bitstring would need a mask parameter, and no executor may default a parameter, so it would have to be a new kind. MEASUREMENT capability.
FAITHFUL: A faithful version needs a genotype that is a structured object with removable parts, an environment that is a set of supplied resources, and a metabolism connecting them, so that removing a part can be compensated by supplying a resource. That is a genome-scale model, not a parameter. It also needs the surrounding hypothesis loop, since a single growth assay in isolation is a measurement and not the Robot Scientist method; the method is the loop that chooses which assay to run next.
REDUCTION: A real one survives, as a two-by-two factorial run entirely on evaluate_bitstring. Fix one world seed and one length L so that all four cells score against the SAME hidden target. Pick an arbitrary candidate bitstring C. Designate a contiguous block K of positions as the gene and a disjoint block S as the supplement. Run four specs: C intact; C with block K forced to all zeros, the knockout; C with block S forced to a fixed pattern, the supplement alone; and C with both, the rescue cell. Each spec carries an ordinary one-scalar outcome rule on score. The interaction, does setting S recover more score when K is zeroed than when it is not, is computed downstream across the four fossils. WHAT IT PRESERVES: the factorial rescue logic; the requirement that all four cells share one environment, which repeat.seed_derivation = constant enforces literally rather than by assumption; and, unexpectedly, the epistemic caveat in the template's own rationale. Because the target is a hash, a block S that raises the score does so for reasons that are genuinely opaque, so a positive rescue in this toy CANNOT be read as saying S is the direct product of K. That turns the alternative-pathway caveat from rhetoric into structure. WHAT IT LOSES: all biology; the pathway graph; dose response; the growth curve and therefore lag and doubling rate; and the entire hypothesis- selection loop that is the actual contribution of the Robot Scientist. WHICH CLAIM IT SUPPORTS: a methodological one about the bench itself, that a bench restricted to one scalar comparison per spec can still detect a two-factor rescue interaction, but only across specs and only with a downstream adjudicator, and that the resulting verdict cannot distinguish direct from indirect rescue. Worth measuring before any real assay backend is wired in, because it fixes what the fossil must carry.

QUESTION: Can an agent that knows nothing about the rules of its environment learn to act well in it, purely by compressing its own past stream of actions and observations and then simulating possible futures from that compressed model?
MECHANISM: The agent runs a closed loop with an environment. At each cycle it emits an action symbol and receives an observation and a reward symbol. The whole history of that stream is fed to a Context Tree Weighting model, which is a Bayesian mixture over all variable order Markov predictors up to a fixed context depth, so the agent does not have to choose a model order. To pick the next action it runs a Monte Carlo tree search, rho-UCT, in which the rollouts are sampled from the CTW mixture itself rather than from a known simulator, out to a finite horizon. It executes the best action, observes what happens, updates the mixture, and repeats for thousands of cycles. Performance is read as average reward per cycle rising over experience, on toy partially observable domains such as a biased coin flip, tiger, a small grid world, tic tac toe and Kuhn poker.
CANDIDATE: The agent itself, more precisely its policy at a given amount of accumulated experience. What is judged is the reward it collects. What varies between agents is the context tree depth, the search horizon and the simulation budget per move.
WORLD: A small partially observable environment that consumes action symbols and emits observation and reward symbols. It supplies hidden state, the transition rules, the observation channel and the reward signal. It must also supply, for normalisation, the random policy score and the optimal policy score.
WHAT_CHANGES: Context tree depth, planning horizon, number of MCTS simulations per move, environment choice and random seed. Critically, experience itself changes within a single run, so the measured quantity is a curve over cycles rather than a value.
MEASURED: Average reward per cycle, continuous, usually rescaled so that the random policy is 0 and the optimal policy is 1. Secondary numbers are model size and time per decision.
INFORMATIVE_FAILURE: Genuinely informative. A failure leaves the learning curve and the fitted CTW model. The depth at which the curve plateaus reports the order of temporal dependency the agent could actually capture, and running the same environment at several depths and several simulation budgets separates a modelling failure, context too shallow to represent the dependency, from a planning failure, too few rollouts to exploit a model that was in fact adequate. That two way split is the useful residue and it survives a total failure to reach optimal reward.
SOURCE_CHECK: VERIFIED. Veness, Ng, Hutter, Uther and Silver, A Monte-Carlo AIXI Approximation, Journal of Artificial Intelligence Research volume 40, 2011. The method combines Context Tree Weighting with a UCT variant on small POMDPs exactly as the template describes, and both named axes, context tree depth and search horizon, are real hyperparameters of that work.
BLOCKER: R-BACKEND: an execution capability. Reference implementations of MC-AIXI-CTW exist as standalone programs, so the bench would only have to launch one, pass the depth, horizon and environment, and fossilize the reward log. What is missing is any executor kind that may invoke an external process, plus any payload field that can name an environment, plus a fossil format for a per cycle reward trace. This is orchestration, not measurement, and the final normalised average reward is a single scalar so the one comparison outcome rule is untouched. R-SUBSTRATE: a state and control flow capability. If the loop is to live inside the bench, the bench needs output to input chaining, because the agent's action is an input to the world and the world's observation is an input to the agent, thousands of times inside one spec. The only stateful kind is random_walk_v0, which accepts no input at all, so there is no path to a closed loop.
FAITHFUL: A faithful version needs an environment registry with a step interface, an agent process holding a mutable model across thousands of cycles within one sealed spec, a per cycle reward log, and per environment random and optimal baselines so the reported scalar is normalised rather than raw. The sealed spec and the single scalar comparison both survive, since the verdict is one number, the normalised average reward over the final block of cycles. What does not survive is one world with a fixed payload and no state.
REDUCTION: A partial reduction exists and it is worth running, but it reaches only one of the two halves of the method. The reachable half is the learning half, the question of whether using history beats not using history. Realise a memoryless agent as a single fixed bitstring evaluated under evaluate_bitstring with seed_derivation sha256_index and count around 200, so every repeat is an independent hidden landscape, that is, an independent environment drawn from a distribution. Its mean score is the no learning baseline and is analytically 0.5. Then have the producer emit a chain of specs against one fixed seed_root, each spec's bits chosen from the fossilized score of the previous spec: that is an agent whose behaviour is a function of its own history, and its score after K specs is the learning curve. Contrast the two at matched evaluation budget K. WHAT IT PRESERVES: the shape of the central claim, that an agent conditioning on its own past outperforms one that does not, on an environment whose rule it was never told; and the budget matched comparison that makes such a claim meaningful. WHAT IT LOSES: partial observability, since the bitstring score is a full and honest report rather than an ambiguous observation; reward per cycle, since there is no cycle; and above all planning, since the scorer has no forward model to roll out, so the horizon_depth axis has no reduction whatsoever and should not be pretended into one. The CTW model class is also gone, so nothing here speaks to compression as induction. WHICH CLAIM: it supports a claim that a history using producer beats a memoryless producer at fixed budget on a hidden target landscape. It does not support any claim about generality, about POMDPs, or about AIXI. NEW DESIGN CHOICE, since both axes are null in the template: context_tree_depth in 16, 32, 48 and horizon_depth in 4 through 8 are reasonable operator settings for a faithful backend run, and are proposed here, not recovered from the source.

QUESTION: Can a language model take a working machine-learning training script, write a modification to it, and have that modification actually run and reach a target validation loss?
MECHANISM: Start from a small working codebase and its known baseline numbers. A language model brainstorms a research idea against that codebase, checks the idea against a literature search for prior art, then a coding agent edits the source files to implement it. The edited code is executed under a fixed compute budget; if it crashes, the error text is fed back and the agent gets a bounded number of repair attempts. Numbers that survive are collected into plots and a write-up, which a second language model then scores. The loop is generate, edit, execute, observe, repair, report.
CANDIDATE: The model-authored code diff, and behind it the idea it encodes. What varies is which idea is attempted; what is judged is whether the diff executes at all and what validation loss the modified script reaches.
WORLD: A concrete template repository plus its dataset, its baseline run, and a wall-clock or GPU budget. The world supplies executability, a loss curve, and a reference baseline to be beaten.
WHAT_CHANGES: idea_id, which selects one of three template codebases, and training_steps, which sets the compute budget per attempt. The parameter values for training_steps were destroyed in ingest and are unknown.
MEASURED: Two things in the real method, which is already a problem for this bench: a boolean execution outcome and a continuous validation loss. The literature also reports a reviewer score on an ordinal scale.
INFORMATIVE_FAILURE: Highly informative. A failed run leaves the exact diff and the exact traceback, which categorize into a real error taxonomy: import and API misuse, shape and dtype errors, silent no-ops where the diff changed nothing on the execution path, and runs that finish but are worse than baseline. That last class is the valuable one, because it separates cannot-implement from implemented-and-useless. A corpus of failing diffs is a reusable artifact even if not one idea ever beats baseline.
SOURCE_CHECK: VERIFIED. The AI Scientist, Lu, Lu, Lange, Foerster, Clune and Ha, 2024, Sakana AI. The three named idea_id choices match the paper's own template set: a nanoGPT language-model template, a grokking template, and a 2D diffusion template. Confirmed from established knowledge, not re-fetched this session.
BLOCKER: R-BACKEND, the missing thing is an execution capability, namely a sandboxed subprocess with a model API and accelerator access that the engine calls and whose diff, stdout and metrics it fossilizes; nothing about bench internals has to change for this; R-EXECUTOR, an adjudication capability is missing, because the honest outcome is a conjunction of executed and loss_at_or_below_target, and the outcome rule is one scalar comparison on one field, so any adapter must collapse the pair into a single field, for example validation loss with a sentinel of positive infinity on crash, and that collapse is a design decision that must be stated in the spec; R-SUBSTRATE, a control-flow capability is missing, since the repair loop feeds the executor's own error output back into its next input, which is output-to-input chaining, and no sealed spec can do that.
FAITHFUL: A faithful implementation needs a real repository, a real dataset, a model endpoint, an isolated writable checkout per attempt, and a bounded repair loop with the traceback as input. It must fossilize the diff, the environment lockfile and the full log alongside the metric, or the run is not reproducible. It also needs a contamination control, because all three named templates are public and a model may have memorized both the code and the known good modifications to it.
REDUCTION: A reduction exists but it is a null-world instrument check, not a capability test, and it must be labelled as such. Freeze one world seed and one length, say length 64 as a NEW DESIGN CHOICE. Tell a language model the exact scoring rule, including that the target is derived by hashing the seed together with the length, and ask it for one bitstring. Seal that bitstring as the bits payload of an evaluate_bitstring spec. Run a matched spec with a uniformly random bitstring of the same length on the same seed. Repeat across many seeds using linear_index repeats, and across several lengths using separate specs. WHAT IT PRESERVES: the outer discipline of the AI Scientist loop that Prometheus actually cares about, which is propose, seal, execute, score, fossilize, with the proposal committed before the target can be seen; and it supplies the one control the real system lacks, because a hash-derived target cannot appear in any training corpus, so the null is exactly a fair-coin match rate and contamination is impossible by construction. WHAT IT LOSES: everything that makes the method a method, namely code, compilation, training dynamics, the repair loop and the reviewer. It also loses the fact that real machine-learning landscapes have exploitable structure while a hash target has none, so a model that is genuinely good at ideas cannot show it here. WHICH CLAIM: only a negative one, that model-authored sealed candidates score at chance on an unmemorizable target. If they do not, the producer pipeline is leaking the target, and the leak is found before an expensive backend is built on top of it. Worth running first, and honestly all this reduction can support.

QUESTION: When two elementary lambda-calculus combinators are applied to one another, does the resulting expression settle into a stable final form within a bounded number of rewriting steps, or does it keep rewriting forever?
MECHANISM: In Fontana's algorithmic chemistry, molecules are lambda terms and a chemical reaction is a collision. Pick two terms A and B from a reactor, form the application of A to B, then beta-reduce that application under a fixed reduction strategy, counting steps. If a normal form is reached before the step ceiling, the normal form is the product and it is injected back into the reactor, displacing a randomly chosen term. If the ceiling is hit first, the collision is declared elastic and nothing is produced. Iterating collisions over a well-stirred population is what eventually yields self-maintaining organizations; the single collision is the atomic event underneath all of that.
CANDIDATE: The ordered pair of combinators, left operand and right operand, drawn from I, K and S, together with the reduction budget. What is judged is whether that specific application halts and what term it halts on.
WORLD: An untyped lambda calculus with a fixed reduction order and a step ceiling. The world supplies the rewriting rules, the notion of a redex, the normal-form test, and the cutoff that turns non-termination into a decidable outcome.
WHAT_CHANGES: Which combinator sits on the left, which sits on the right, and max_reductions over the range 10 to 1000.
MEASURED: A halting boolean, an integer count of reduction steps consumed, and a term-valued product. Steps are on a bounded integer scale; the product is symbolic and not a number at all.
INFORMATIVE_FAILURE: Useful. A collision that exhausts its budget names exactly which ordered pair diverges, and that catalogue of inert, productive and divergent pairs IS the reaction table of the chemistry. There is a second and sharper informative failure available here, and it fires before any code runs. Over the nine ordered pairs drawn from I, K and S, every application is either already in normal form because K and S are partially applied and contain no redex, or it reduces in a single step because I is applied to something. Nothing in this param space can consume more than one reduction. So the max_reductions axis from 10 to 1000 is inert across its entire range, and the template is degenerate by construction. That is the most valuable thing this template produces and it costs nothing to find.
SOURCE_CHECK: PLAUSIBLE. Fontana and Buss 1994 "The arrival of the fittest: toward a theory of biological organization" is a real paper and is the canonical statement of levels of self-maintaining organization in lambda-calculus chemistry, but the specific collide-and-beta-reduce operator described here is more precisely Fontana's earlier algorithmic-chemistry work; web search budget was exhausted this session and the exact attribution of the collision rule could not be confirmed.
BLOCKER: R-EXECUTOR: missing measurement and missing control flow. No kind performs term rewriting, no kind can loop until a fixed point subject to a budget, and no kind can return a symbolic term as a result field. R-REPAIR: not a capability gap at all. The combinator alphabet I, K, S is a degenerate parameter choice whose whole range collapses the budget axis; the alphabet must be widened to terms with real reduction depth, for example self-application terms, before the experiment can discriminate anything. R-SUBSTRATE: missing state. Any claim about organization needs a reactor that reinjects products, which is output-to-input chaining plus a persistent population.
FAITHFUL: A beta-reduction engine over untyped lambda terms with a pluggable reduction order, a step counter, and a normal-form test, returning halted, steps and the normal-form term. The spec must be able to carry two term-valued payload fields and return a term-valued result, neither of which the current payload shapes allow. To say anything about self-maintaining organization on top of that, a population reactor with reinjection is required, which is a separate substrate capability.
REDUCTION: A real one survives, and it keeps the actual question rather than the lambda calculus. The question underneath is: does repeated application of an operator to its own output reach a stable form within a budget, and is that budget axis live or inert? The bench already contains one operator with exactly that shape, because evaluate_bitstring derives its hidden target from the seed and the length. Fix a length L. Define the producer-side map f taking a seed to the integer whose binary expansion is the hidden target at that seed and length L. Then chain: seed_0, f of seed_0, f of f of seed_0, and so on, one spec per application, each spec a trivial evaluate_bitstring whose returned bits expose the target. Measure the transient length before the sequence enters a cycle, and the cycle length, subject to a chain-length budget that plays the role of max_reductions. PRESERVES: iterated self-application of a deterministic operator, a halting-or-not verdict decided by a budget, the budget as the primary axis, and the seed-to-seed variation in transient length that makes the statistic non-trivial. LOSES: lambda calculus entirely, the structure of the product, any notion of a reactor or of self-maintaining organization, and therefore every claim the field cares about. CLAIM SUPPORTED: that halting-within-budget under iterated self-application has a measurable, seed-dependent distribution with a non-degenerate budget axis, and by direct contrast, that the template as written does not, since f-chaining on a hash is a near-permutation whose transients are short and whose budget axis is nearly as inert as the I, K, S alphabet. That contrast is the finding worth having before an executor is built. NEW DESIGN CHOICE: L equals 16, chain budget 256, 200 seed_0 values.

QUESTION: Can a search over encoded sequences of computational primitives find a genome that behaves like a target algorithm, rather than merely resembling it bit for bit?
MECHANISM: In the PADO line of work, a genome is decoded into an executable program, in that case a graph or tree of primitive operations with indexed memory. The program is then run on a set of input signals, its outputs are read, and fitness is the quality of those outputs on the classification task. Multiple such programs are orchestrated, each contributing a confidence, and the ensemble decides. The essential step is that the genome is INTERPRETED before it is judged; nothing is scored on its syntax.
CANDIDATE: The bitstring genome. What varies across specs is which bitstring is submitted and, through length, which landscape it faces. What is being judged, on this bench, is the fraction of positions matching a hidden target string.
WORLD: One integer seed, from which the executor derives a hidden target of the declared length by hashing the string target, the seed and the length. The world supplies nothing else: no inputs, no interpreter, no task.
WHAT_CHANGES: Across the given param_space only the choice between two structured 16-bit candidates, period-2 alternation and period-4 blocks, plus the length axis, which arrived null. Across specs the seed also varies, which redraws the landscape entirely.
MEASURED: score, continuous from 0 to 1, equal to the count of matching positions divided by the target length, plus solved, a boolean true only at score 1.0.
INFORMATIVE_FAILURE: Thin as an algorithm result but sharp as an instrument result. A low score tells you nothing about algorithmic quality because nothing was executed. What a run does leave behind is a sample from the chance distribution of a structured string against a hash-derived target, which accumulates into the bench's own null and is reusable by every later bitstring template. A repeated near-0.5 result across many seeds is the useful finding that the hash target is unbiased with respect to low-complexity strings.
SOURCE_CHECK: PLAUSIBLE. Astro Teller's PADO is real and was developed with Manuela Veloso at Carnegie Mellon; search returns a 1995 CMU technical report, PADO, learning tree structured algorithms for orchestration into an object recognition system, and related 1995 to 1997 papers on algorithm evolution for signal understanding. The acronym is expanded as Parallel Architecture Discovery and Orchestration in some sources and Parallel Algorithm Discovery and Orchestration in others, and no publication with exactly the cited title and year 1996 was confirmed, so the method is real but this specific attribution is not established.
BLOCKER: R-REPAIR is blocked only on a missing parameter, the null length axis, which is a specification gap and not a capability gap; R-COMPOSE is blocked on adjudication, because the ensemble statement over many seeds is an aggregation the single scalar outcome rule cannot express and must be read downstream; R-EXECUTOR is blocked on a measurement capability, since nothing on the bench can decode a genome into operations, run it on inputs, and return output quality, and that is the entire method.

Orchestration of several programs is a second layer and can wait. Without the interpreter the template is a bitstring similarity test wearing an algorithm-discovery label.
REDUCTION: This template is already executable, and the reduction is to stop pretending it is about algorithms and use it as instrument calibration. Set length to 16, which is a REPAIR and not a design choice, because both supplied candidates are exactly 16 characters long. This matters more than it looks: the scorer divides matches by the TARGET length while comparing only over the overlap, so a 16-character candidate against length 32 has a maximum attainable score of 0.5 and any threshold above that can never fire. Then run both candidates across many seeds under sha256_index or linear_index repeats, never under constant with state reset and count above 1, which the bench flags as degenerate by construction. WHAT IT PRESERVES: fixed candidate scored against a hidden target derived from the world, and the contrast between two candidates of different periodicity. WHAT IT LOSES: interpretation, execution, inputs, outputs and orchestration, that is the whole of PADO. WHICH CLAIM IT SUPPORTS: that the hidden-target hash is unbiased with respect to structured low-complexity bitstrings, tested as an empirical mean against the exact binomial null with mean 0.5 and standard deviation 1 over 2 root L, which for L equal to 16 is 0.125. That is a genuine bench-hygiene result and is available today at near zero cost.

QUESTION: If you put one hand-written self-copying program into a block of computer memory and let copying make occasional mistakes, does an ecology appear on its own, including creatures that live off other creatures?
MECHANISM: A region of virtual memory, the soup, is seeded with a single ancestor written in a purpose-built machine code, roughly eighty instructions long, whose whole job is to measure itself, allocate space and copy itself into it. A scheduler gives each running creature slices of CPU time. Errors are injected in two places, as background bit flips in the soup and as mistakes during copying. When memory fills, a reaper queue kills the oldest and the most error-prone creatures to make room. Nothing selects for anything in particular: the only currencies are memory space and CPU time, so whatever copies itself faster in the space available takes over. What is observed is that shorter creatures appear which have lost the copy loop and instead execute a neighbour's copy code, that is, parasites; then hosts that resist them; then hyper-parasites; then creatures that cheat cooperative arrangements.
CANDIDATE: A creature, that is, a contiguous block of executable instructions with its own instruction pointer. What varies is its length and its exact instruction sequence. It is judged by nothing external: it is judged by whether copies of it are still in memory later.
WORLD: A shared, mutable memory arena with a CPU scheduler and a reaper. The world supplies exactly two scarce resources, space and time, and one genotype-phenotype map, the instruction set, which decides what a mutated instruction sequence actually does.
WHAT_CHANGES: Soup size and mutation rate across runs; within a run, the contents of memory, the length distribution of creatures and the lineage tree, all of which change continuously.
MEASURED: A time series rather than a scalar: the histogram of creature lengths over time, the number of distinct genotypes, the lineage tree, and the appearance time of the first creature that cannot replicate in isolation, which is the operational definition of a parasite.
INFORMATIVE_FAILURE: A run in which nothing but the ancestor ever persists is a measurement of the INSTRUCTION SET rather than of evolution: it says the ancestor sits in a mutational neighbourhood that is almost entirely lethal, and the run hands you the lethal fraction, the neutral fraction, and the specific instructions whose mutation kills. That is a reusable property of the substrate and it is arguably the more valuable of the two outcomes, because it is the number that predicts whether any related design will work.
SOURCE_CHECK: VERIFIED. Ray, T. S., An Approach to the Synthesis of Life, in Artificial Life II, Addison-Wesley, 1991, is the correct and canonical reference for Tierra, the memory soup, the roughly eighty-instruction ancestor, the reaper, and the emergence of parasites and hyper-parasites. This one was not re-checked online because the session's web-search budget was exhausted; the attribution is standard and unambiguous in the ALife literature.
BLOCKER: R-BACKEND is missing an execution-backend capability, an adapter that runs an external simulator binary under a declared seed and captures its output stream as a fossilised result; this is the cheap route and it is not hypothetical, since the repository already carries an ergon/avida2003 tree and previously recovered mid-1990s digital-evolution genomes verified by execution. R-SUBSTRATE is missing a state capability, specifically a shared mutable arena persisting across a whole run and, harder, inter-candidate access, since one creature must be able to execute another's memory. R-WORLD is missing a world capability: one integer seed_root is the entire world, and there is no population, no arena, no scheduler and no reaper.
FAITHFUL: A faithful version needs a persistent memory arena, a time-slicing scheduler over many concurrently executing programs, an instruction set with a real genotype-phenotype map, mutation applied both to stored memory and to copy operations, and a reaper. The observation is a time series and a lineage tree rather than one number, so the outcome rule would have to adjudicate a derived scalar computed downstream, for instance the appearance time of the first non-self-sufficient replicator.
REDUCTION: NONE, and the reason is specific rather than general. Tierra's whole content lives in the genotype-phenotype map: a bit flip changes an instruction, which changes what a program DOES, which is why mutations can be lethal, neutral or parasitic. The bench's only landscape has no genotype-phenotype map at all, because score is the fraction of positions matching a hidden target, so every position contributes independently and additively. Consequently the obvious reduction, submit an ancestor word plus all of its single-bit mutants and profile the neighbourhood, measures a constant that is known before the run: exactly L minus m of the L flips improve the score by 1/L and m of them worsen it by 1/L, where m is the count of already-matching positions, and the neutral fraction is identically zero. It cannot detect lethality, neutrality, robustness or evolvability, because none of those exist on an additive landscape. Separately, no reduction on this bench can produce a parasite at all, because a parasite is one candidate executing another candidate's code and a spec contains exactly one candidate with no means of referring to a second. WHAT SURVIVES SHORT OF THE METHOD, and it is worth building: the bench is the correct NULL ARM for an external run. If Tierra or Avida is run under R-BACKEND, the matching-fraction landscape answers the question what does mutation plus selection achieve when the genotype-phenotype map is the identity, which is the baseline any claim of emergent complexity has to beat. That is a control for this template, not an instance of it, and it must be labelled as such.

QUESTION: Can a hand-written program, running in a shared block of computer memory, copy itself successfully? This is the sanity check you run before turning mutation on and seeing what evolves.
MECHANISM: Reserve a large block of memory, the soup. Write one ancestor program in a machine language designed so that most random edits still produce something that runs: no numeric operands, and addressing by matching templates of no-operation instructions rather than by absolute address, so the code survives being moved. The ancestor's body is a loop that measures its own length by locating its start and end templates, requests a fresh block of memory from the operating system, copies itself instruction by instruction into that block, and issues a divide instruction that hands the daughter block its own instruction pointer and slice of CPU time. A scheduler round-robins CPU time across all living creatures. A reaper kills creatures when memory fills, preferring the old and the error-prone. That combination, self-copy plus finite memory plus a reaper, is what turns replication rate into a selection pressure. In the full experiment a mutation operator flips bits in the soup and during copying, and parasites appear that lack a copy loop and execute their neighbours' instead.
CANDIDATE: The ancestor program, a sequence of instructions. What varies is the instruction sequence and the machine language it is written in.
WORLD: The soup: a finite, addressable, MUTABLE shared memory, plus a scheduler granting execution slices and a reaper removing creatures. The environment supplies memory as the limiting resource, CPU time as the currency, and death. Other creatures are part of the world, which is why the world is also an ecology.
WHAT_CHANGES: Across runs, the ancestor's instruction set and length, the soup size, and the number of cycles the simulation is allowed to run.
MEASURED: For the baseline question, a fact: did the ancestor produce at least one viable daughter, and does the population sustain itself. Scalar proxies are population count at cycle N, generations elapsed, or fraction of soup occupied. All are continuous or count-valued and all require the simulation to have run to completion.
INFORMATIVE_FAILURE: Concretely informative, though it is a debugging signal more than a scientific one. If the ancestor fails to replicate you learn that the instruction set as specified is not closed under the operations the copy loop needs, or that template addressing does not resolve, or that the allocator refuses the daughter. Each points at a specific missing primitive. The stronger informative failure comes later: if replication works but the population collapses, you have learned that the reaper and scheduler parameters, not the genome, set viability, which is a claim about the world rather than the organism.
SOURCE_CHECK: VERIFIED - Thomas S. Ray, An Approach to the Synthesis of Life, in Artificial Life II, 1991, is the correct primary reference for Tierra and covers the ancestor, the soup, the reaper, template addressing and the emergence of parasites. Caveat on the parameter axis: the choices are named 80_tierran_opcodes and 82_tierran_opcodes, which appears to conflate two different quantities. The canonical ancestor is roughly eighty INSTRUCTIONS LONG, whereas the Tierran instruction SET is far smaller, on the order of thirty-two opcodes. If the axis means ancestor length it is misnamed; if it means opcode-set size the values are wrong. Flag for the operator. I could not re-verify the exact counts against the paper because the search budget was spent.
BLOCKER: R-BACKEND - nothing missing in principle; Tierra and its descendants are real, runnable, published programs, and the bench would only have to invoke one, pass the seed and parameters, and fossilize a scalar from its log. MEASUREMENT capability only, and cheap. R-EXECUTOR - for the reduced self-copy version the bench needs a kind that executes an instruction sequence over a writable tape and returns a fidelity scalar. MEASUREMENT capability. R-SUBSTRATE - for the real thing the bench lacks mutable shared memory persisting across creatures, a scheduler, creature birth and death, and a population at all. STATE AND CONTROL-FLOW capability, and this is the substantive blocker: one world is one integer, and there is nowhere to put a soup.
FAITHFUL: A faithful version needs a mutable addressable memory that outlives any single evaluation, an interpreter that can write into it, a scheduler interleaving many instruction pointers, and a death rule. It needs the world to hold a population rather than a seed, so the world object itself changes type. And it needs long runs, millions of cycles, so the fossil must summarise a trajectory rather than a returned value.
REDUCTION: Two layers, one honest and small, one a gesture I recommend against. The gesture to avoid: mapping soup occupancy onto random_walk_v0's position and calling the walk a population. Nothing about replication survives that. The walk has no copying, no memory to copy into, and its increments do not depend on its state. It would produce a number that looks like a population curve and means nothing. The reduction that does survive addresses exactly the question this template actually asks, which is pre-mutation viability of one written ancestor, not evolution. Define a tiny copy machine: a fixed-length tape, a read head and a write head, and six opcodes - advance-read, advance-write, copy-byte, jump-if-template, allocate, divide. Supply the instruction sequence as the payload. Run it for a bounded number of cycles against a fresh daughter region and return ONE scalar, the fraction of the daughter tape matching the parent. That is continuous in the range zero to one and drops straight into a single-comparison outcome rule with no change to the rule engine. Under repeat.seed_derivation = sha256_index each repeat can randomise the daughter's start offset, which tests the template-addressing property that is the actual insight of Tierran machine code: whether the copy loop still works when the code is not where it expects to be. That property is what makes the language robust to mutation, and it can be measured with no mutation, no population and no ecology at all. WHAT IT PRESERVES: self-copying as an executed act rather than an asserted one, copy fidelity as a continuous measurement, and position independence, which is the real design claim of the substrate. WHAT IT LOSES: the soup, the reaper, the scheduler, competition for CPU time, mutation, parasites, and open-endedness. Everything ecological. WHICH CLAIM IT SUPPORTS: only that a given instruction set is or is not closed under self-copy and is or is not position independent. That is a substrate-viability claim, and it is the correct first claim, but it must never be reported as an evolution result.

QUESTION: Can a program that starts from a handful of elementary set theory ideas and a bag of rules of thumb invent new mathematical concepts that a mathematician would call interesting?
MECHANISM: AM holds each concept as a frame with slots, a definition, known examples, generalisations, specialisations and a numeric worth. It also holds an agenda of pending tasks, each task being something like fill in examples of this concept, generalise it, specialise it, or look for a regularity among its examples. The agenda is sorted by an interestingness score computed from heuristic rules. The loop is: pop the top task, run it, which usually means executing or rewriting a Lisp definition, create whatever new concepts result, assign them a worth, and push the tasks they suggest back onto the agenda. Run until the step budget is spent. Famously the loop reached the notion of a number with unusually few divisors, that is, primes, and then unique factorisation, from set theoretic starting material. The output is not one number, it is the trace of concepts created and their worth.
CANDIDATE: A generated concept, that is, a Lisp frame carrying an executable definition. What varies is which concepts get created and what worth the heuristics award them.
WORLD: An initial concept library, a heuristic rule set, an agenda and a representation language. The environment supplies the starting concepts, the Lisp representation in which mutations of a definition are usually still meaningful, and the worth function that decides what interesting means.
WHAT_CHANGES: The number of initial concepts, the agenda step budget, which heuristics are enabled or ablated, and tie breaking order.
MEASURED: The count of concepts generated whose worth exceeds a threshold, on a bounded numeric scale, plus a discrete rediscovery checklist, did it reach primes, did it reach unique factorisation. The second of those is the number anyone actually cares about and it is not continuous.
INFORMATIVE_FAILURE: Strongly informative, and this is a case where the failure is more valuable than the success. A run that produces nothing interesting still yields the full concept trace, which can be read to see where the generative pressure died. More importantly, an ablation over heuristics answers the question that AM's own author later raised, namely whether the apparent discovery is carried by the heuristics at all or by the fact that in Lisp a syntactic mutation of a definition is very often still a meaningful definition. A failure that isolates the representation as the load bearing part is a real result about machine discovery.
SOURCE_CHECK: VERIFIED, with a dating note. AM is Lenat's 1976 Stanford doctoral thesis, AM: An Artificial Intelligence Approach to Discovery in Mathematics as Heuristic Search; the item usually cited as Lenat 1977 is the IJCAI-77 paper on automated theory formation in mathematics. The system, the agenda, the heuristics and the frame representation are as described, so the method and attribution are right and only the year is ambiguous between thesis and conference paper.
BLOCKER: R-SUBSTRATE: a state capability. AM is an archive that grows and whose contents become the inputs of later steps. The bench fixes the payload for the whole spec, so a spec can never add a concept to its own inputs. Missing: a persistent archive plus output to input chaining within one spec. R-EXECUTOR: a measurement capability. Nothing in the bench can evaluate a symbolic definition, enumerate its examples, or compute a worth score. That needs an interpreter that returns a scalar. R-BACKEND: an execution capability. Existing theory formation systems in the AM lineage could be driven from outside and their concept traces fossilized. What is missing is an external process executor and a fossil format for a concept trace, not a measurement.
FAITHFUL: A faithful version needs an executable concept representation, an interpreter that can produce examples from a definition, an agenda whose ordering is computed by heuristics that rewrite concepts, and a worth function; and it needs all of that to persist and mutate inside a single experiment. The one scalar outcome rule can survive, since the verdict can be the count of concepts above a worth threshold, but the sealed fixed payload cannot.
REDUCTION: Two reductions, one runnable now across specs and one small executor away. First, the search dynamics half, runnable on the current bench through the producer. Represent a concept as a fixed length bitstring and worth as its evaluate_bitstring score against one hidden target, holding seed_root and seed_derivation constant across every spec so all arms face the same landscape. The producer keeps an archive of the highest scoring bitstrings seen so far and emits each new spec's bits as a recombination or mutation of two archive members. The control producer emits uniformly random bits at the same spec budget. Agenda steps map onto spec count. WHAT IT PRESERVES: AM's actual search dynamic, that recombining already valued objects finds valued objects faster than sampling fresh ones, together with the budget axis and a real archive. WHAT IT LOSES: everything symbolic. There are no definitions, nothing is executable, and therefore the reduction is blind to precisely the property Lenat later identified as load bearing, namely that mutating a Lisp definition usually yields another meaningful definition. It also loses interestingness, since a hidden target score is a fixed objective and AM's worth function is itself heuristic and revisable. WHICH CLAIM: it supports a claim about archive driven recombination beating blind sampling at fixed budget. It cannot support any claim about concept formation. Second, the representation half, one small executor away and much more faithful. Let the bits encode a tiny expression over a fixed grammar, and let the score be the fraction of a hidden truth table the decoded expression reproduces. Now a mutation of the string is a mutation of a program, and the measurable quantity is what fraction of mutations remain meaningful, which is the actual AM question, stated as a measurement rather than a demonstration. That is R-EXECUTOR and it is small, an interpreter for a grammar of ten or so operators. NEW DESIGN CHOICE, since both axes are null: initial_concepts 8, agenda_steps 200, bitstring length 32. Proposed here, not recovered from the source.

QUESTION: If an agent is rewarded for surprising itself, does it seek out the parts of its world it does not yet understand, and does it lose interest once it has learned them?
MECHANISM: Two networks share a world. A model network watches the current state and the action taken and tries to predict the next state; it is trained to reduce its own prediction error. A controller network chooses actions and is rewarded by exactly that prediction error, so it is trained to increase it. The two are in direct opposition. The consequence is a moving target: a region that is initially surprising pulls the controller toward it, the model learns that region, the error falls, and the controller leaves. That departure is boredom, and it falls out of the arithmetic rather than being programmed. The known failure is a region whose unpredictability is irreducible, such as pure noise, where the model can never reduce error and the controller never leaves.
CANDIDATE: The controller, judged by where in the world it spends its time and whether that allocation tracks the model's residual error.
WORLD: An environment with observations, an action interface, and temporal structure, so that a next state exists to be predicted. The environment supplies both learnable regularity and, in the interesting version, at least one region of irreducible noise.
WHAT_CHANGES: hidden_units, which sets model capacity and therefore what counts as learnable, and delayed_reward_steps, which sets how far ahead the prediction reaches. Both parameter value sets were destroyed in ingest.
MEASURED: Prediction error over time, on a continuous scale, and the controller's occupancy over regions, as a distribution. The claim lives in the coupling between the two, not in either one alone.
INFORMATIVE_FAILURE: Useful. If the controller parks permanently in the noisy region, that is the noisy-television result and it is a positive finding about the drive rather than a null. If prediction error falls to zero everywhere with no change in occupancy, the environment had no differential structure to find, which indicts the world and not the agent. The one failure that leaves nothing behind is a controller that never learns at all, because then occupancy says nothing about the drive.
SOURCE_CHECK: VERIFIED. Schmidhuber, A possibility for implementing curiosity and boredom in model-building neural controllers, in the 1991 Simulation of Adaptive Behavior proceedings. The dual-network arrangement, the reward on the model's prediction error, and the explicit treatment of boredom are all in that work. Confirmed from established knowledge.
BLOCKER: R-COMPOSE, an adjudication capability is missing for the full claim, because the finding is a relation between an error curve and an occupancy distribution while the outcome rule is one scalar comparison, so any verdict must be computed downstream and the specs can carry only raw observations; R-WORLD, the missing thing is the world itself, specifically an action interface, since neither existing kind lets anything choose what to do next inside a run, and without actions there is no controller; R-SUBSTRATE, a state capability is missing, namely learner weights that persist and update across steps, plus output-to-input chaining so the model's error becomes the controller's reward; R-BACKEND, no capability of substance is missing, an existing reinforcement-learning library could run this and the bench would only have to call it and fossilize the curves.
FAITHFUL: A faithful implementation needs a small environment with actions and observations, two trainable modules with persistent parameters, and a reward wire from the model's error to the controller. It must contain at least one learnable region and one irreducibly stochastic region, or the boredom claim and the noise-trap claim cannot be separated. Error and occupancy must be logged per step, not only at the end.
REDUCTION: A good reduction exists, and it turns on a bench property that was not designed for it. Drop the controller and keep the drive signal. Treat each world seed as a region and each evaluate_bitstring call as one observation of that region. Have a producer-side predictor forecast the score of the next probe bitstring in a region, and define the curiosity signal as the absolute error of that forecast. Now use repeat.seed_derivation as the learnability switch, which is the whole trick. Under constant, every repeat scores against the SAME hidden target, the region is a fixed function, and a predictor that has seen enough probes drives its error toward zero, which is boredom observed directly. Under sha256_index, every repeat scores against a DIFFERENT target, the region is redrawn each time, and no predictor can push its error below the spread of the score distribution, which is exactly the noisy television. Run both arms at matched probe counts, say 200 probes per arm as a NEW DESIGN CHOICE, and compare error trajectories offline. WHAT IT PRESERVES: the heterostatic signal itself, the distinction between reducible and irreducible uncertainty, the decay of interest, and the trap, which is precisely the failure mode the template's own rationale says a SURVIVED verdict would not license. WHAT IT LOSES: the controller, and therefore the closed loop. Nothing chooses where to go, so this measures the drive signal and not the agent. It also loses the adversarial coupling, since the predictor has no opponent. WHICH CLAIM: that prediction-error-as-drive separates learnable from irreducible variance, and by how much, on a landscape whose irreducibility is known by construction rather than assumed. That is a genuine calibration of the signal, and it is the precondition for trusting it inside a controller later.

QUESTION: Starting from a small set of given concepts and a finite pile of example objects, how many non-trivial conjectures does an automated concept-inventing loop actually produce within a fixed search budget, and does narrowing the set of ways it is allowed to build new concepts change that yield?
MECHANISM: HR begins with core concepts and concrete example data, for example the integers up to some bound or a set of small finite groups. Production rules such as exists, match, negate, size, split and compose take existing concepts and manufacture new concept definitions. Every new concept is evaluated empirically by computing its extension, the set of example objects that satisfy it. Regularities among extensions are then read off as conjectures: two concepts with identical extensions give an equivalence conjecture, one extension contained in another gives an implication, an empty extension gives a non-existence conjecture. Concepts are scored by interestingness measures and the best are fed back to the production rules, so the theory is an archive that grows and reshapes what gets built next.
CANDIDATE: The invented concept, that is a definition assembled by applying a production rule to concepts already in the theory. It is judged twice, first empirically by its extension over the object set and second by interestingness heuristics that decide whether it re-enters the generator.
WORLD: A finite set of example objects plus the initial axioms and core concepts. The world's essential contribution is ground truth extensions: every conjecture is checked against actual objects, so the loop is empirical rather than deductive.
WHAT_CHANGES: Number of initial axioms, unknown because the source destroyed the value. Production rule set, full versus restrictive. Number of search steps, also unknown.
MEASURED: A count of emitted conjectures, a non-negative integer, ideally broken down by conjecture class. Secondarily the size and shape of the concept tree.
INFORMATIVE_FAILURE: Strongly informative, and this is one of the better failure modes in the chunk. If yield collapses, what remains is the concept tree itself: which production rules fired, which produced concepts whose extensions duplicated an existing concept, which produced empty or full extensions, and where branching stopped. That is a direct map of where the generator's menu ran out, which is the bounded-menu question rather than a nuisance. A high yield under the restrictive rule set together with a low yield under the full set would be positive evidence that most of the full set's output is duplicate re-derivation, which is a result about the generator and not about mathematics.
SOURCE_CHECK: VERIFIED. Colton 2002 "Automated Theory Formation in Pure Mathematics" is confirmed in DBLP as a Springer Distinguished Dissertations volume by Simon Colton, and it is the standard reference for the HR system's theory-formation loop.
BLOCKER: R-COMPOSE: missing adjudication. The producer can hold the theory and count conjectures downstream, but the outcome rule is one field, one operator, one value on a single spec, so a yield count aggregated over many specs cannot be adjudicated by the bench, only recorded. R-SUBSTRATE: missing state. The theory is an archive that grows during a run and each step's output is the next step's input; there is no archive and no output-to-input chaining. R-EXECUTOR: missing measurement. There is no concept datatype, no extension evaluator, and no result field that can carry a set or a count of emitted objects. R-REPAIR: initial_axioms and search_steps are null and must be chosen before admission; the axis names are real, the numbers are not recoverable.
FAITHFUL: A typed concept or definition datatype closed under a production-rule set, an extension evaluator over a fixed finite object set, a persistent theory store with an interestingness ranking, and a conjecture-emission predicate over pairs of extensions. The spec must be able to return a list of conjecture objects and a count, and the outcome must be able to threshold an aggregate, both of which the sealed one-scalar-comparison model forbids.
REDUCTION: A genuinely faithful small version exists, using the bitstring scorer as the extension oracle. Fix a length L. Define a concept as a mask, that is a subset of the L positions, and define its extension operationally as the score returned when the producer submits the bitstring that is all zeros except ones on the mask. Production rules are union, intersection and complement over two existing masks; the restrictive rule set is union only. The producer runs the HR loop outside the bench, one spec per concept, and the bench acts purely as the empirical world. A conjecture is an observed equality of extension between two concepts, and the crucial move is to use sha256_index repeats so that each repeat scores against an independent hidden target: an equality that survives across thirty independent landscapes is a structural fact about the mask algebra, not an accident of one target. Yield is then conjectures surviving per hundred concepts generated, measured under the full rule set and under the restrictive one. PRESERVES: concept invention by composition, empirical evaluation of extensions against real objects, conjecture as surviving regularity rather than proved statement, the yield-per-budget statistic, and the full-versus-restrictive contrast. LOSES: logic, quantification, mathematical objects, interestingness heuristics, and any claim that a conjecture is true rather than merely unfalsified over the sampled landscapes. CLAIM SUPPORTED: that production-rule breadth changes the rate of surviving empirical regularities per unit of search, and specifically that a large share of a broad generator's yield is duplicate re-derivation. PRE-REGISTERED NULL, and it must be computed before anything is frozen: on a hash target the score of a mask bitstring is essentially a function of mask cardinality alone, so almost every discovered equality will be explained by equal mask size. The only admissible conjectures are those that survive after conditioning on cardinality, and if none do, the reduction has shown that this substrate carries no structure for a conjecture generator to find, which is itself the useful answer. NEW DESIGN CHOICE: L equals 24, 30 sha256_index repeats, 400 concepts per rule set.

QUESTION: Can a small set of general heuristics, applied to a table of measurements, rediscover the empirical law that generated them, without being told the form of the law in advance?
MECHANISM: BACON reads a table of observed variables. It applies a handful of data-driven heuristics, one at a time. If a quantity is constant, record it as a law. If two quantities increase together, define a new theoretical term equal to their ratio. If one increases as the other decreases, define their product. Each new term becomes a column in the table, and the heuristics run again on the enlarged table. The recursion halts when some derived term comes out constant within tolerance, and that constant term is the discovered law. This is how BACON reaches expressions of the same shape as the ideal gas law and Kepler's third law from raw tables.
CANDIDATE: A derived theoretical term, that is a composed expression over the observed variables. What varies is which composition the heuristics build. What is judged is whether that term is constant across the rows within tolerance.
WORLD: A data table produced by some underlying process, plus a noise level. The world supplies the observed variables, their ranges, and the measurement error that sets the tolerance for calling something constant.
WHAT_CHANGES: The number of variables in the table and the depth to which the heuristics are allowed to recurse before giving up. Both axes arrived null. Noise level is the axis the rationale cares about and it is not in the param_space at all.
MEASURED: Whether a law was found within the depth budget, the depth at which it was found, and the residual variation of the discovered constant. The natural scalar is the residual, from 0 upward.
INFORMATIVE_FAILURE: Useful. A failure at a given depth is a lower bound on the compositional complexity of the true law with respect to that heuristic set, which is a real statement about the data and not just about the run. The partial table of derived terms is also kept, and the terms that came closest to constant are directional pointers toward the right composition. Failure here narrows the search space rather than emptying it.
SOURCE_CHECK: VERIFIED. Pat Langley's BACON is a well established production system for discovering empirical laws, first reported in 1977 and developed through BACON.1 to BACON.5 and the Scientific Discovery volume with Simon, Bradshaw and Zytkow. Confirmation here rests on established literature knowledge rather than a fetch, because the session web search budget was exhausted; the method and the attribution to Langley are not in doubt, the exact 1977 venue was not re-checked.

It must also record the discovered expression itself, because the residual alone cannot distinguish the true law from an accidental invariant.
REDUCTION: A good one exists and it uses the walk as a data generator rather than the bitstring as a candidate. random_walk_v0 is a genuine stochastic process with a known governing law: each step is uniform on minus step_scale to plus step_scale, so displacement has mean 0 and variance equal to steps times step_scale squared over 3. Run a grid of specs sweeping steps over 10, 30, 100, 300, 1000 and step_scale over 0.1, 1.0, 10.0, many seeds each, all under sha256_index so the repeats are independent draws. Then, downstream and outside the outcome rule, apply BACON's own heuristics to the resulting table whose columns are steps, step_scale and squared displacement, and see whether the ratio heuristic recovers a constant, which it should, at the value one third. NEW DESIGN CHOICE: the grid above, and heuristic depth 3, since both axes arrived null. WHAT IT PRESERVES: everything except the identity of the data source. A real generating process, a planted law that is known exactly in advance, genuine measurement noise from finite sampling, term composition by ratio, and a constancy test at a declared tolerance. WHAT IT LOSES: the richness of a multi-variable physical table, so the discoverable law is a single scaling relation and the recursion never goes past depth 2. WHICH CLAIM IT SUPPORTS: that the bench's fossil record is sufficient to recover a planted scaling law and its constant from observations alone. That is a precondition for every discovery template in the inbox and nobody has checked it.

QUESTION: Before collecting any data at all, how much would a planned study of a given size be expected to teach us, and is that enough to be worth doing?
MECHANISM: Write down what you already believe as a prior distribution over the unknown parameters, and write down how data would be generated from those parameters as a likelihood. For a candidate design, such as a sample size or a set of measurement points, imagine every dataset the design could produce, weighted by how likely each is under your current beliefs. For each imagined dataset compute the posterior you would end up with and measure how far it has moved from the prior, in the Shannon sense. Average that movement over all imagined datasets. The average is the expected information gain, which is the design's utility. Under a conjugate normal model this integral is closed form; otherwise it is estimated by nested Monte Carlo. No data is ever collected.
CANDIDATE: A proposed design, here parameterised by sample size, judged by its expected utility. Nothing is fitted and nothing is observed.
WORLD: An assumed statistical model. It supplies the prior, the prior variance, the likelihood and the measurement noise level. The world here is entirely stipulated, which is at once the method's strength and its exposure.
WHAT_CHANGES: Sample size and prior variance across runs.
MEASURED: Expected information gain, a non-negative continuous quantity in nats or bits, one number per design.
INFORMATIVE_FAILURE: If utility stays under threshold across the whole grid of sample sizes, the failure is diagnostic and not merely negative: it says the design family cannot be rescued by spending more, because the bottleneck is the model or the noise rather than the budget. What is left behind is the utility-versus-sample-size curve, which can be inverted to give the smallest n that would ever suffice, or to prove that no n does.
SOURCE_CHECK: VERIFIED. Chaloner and Verdinelli, Bayesian Experimental Design: A Review, Statistical Science 10(3), 1995, is the standard review and it covers Shannon-information utility and the normal-model closed forms in which prior variance and sample size are the natural axes. The template's axes match the source's own framing.
BLOCKER: R-EXECUTOR is missing a measurement capability and nothing else: no executor accepts a model description and returns a scalar, and no payload schema can carry a prior and a likelihood. Note what is NOT blocking: no state, no control flow, no population, no chaining, and the outcome rule already fits, since expected information gain at least some threshold is exactly one field, one operator, one value. This is among the cheapest templates in the chunk. R-BACKEND is missing an execution-backend capability, an adapter to an existing estimator library. R-COMPOSE is missing an adjudication capability, but only for the robustness question, since comparing utility across several priors is an aggregation across specs.
FAITHFUL: A faithful version needs a payload that can carry a model, that is, a prior with its hyperparameters, a likelihood family and a design, and an executor returning expected information gain either in closed form for the conjugate case or by nested Monte Carlo otherwise, with the estimator's own bias reported beside the estimate. It is stateless and single-scalar, so it requires no substrate change at all.
REDUCTION: A real information-gain measurement is available today with no new executor, because the bench already contains a hidden quantity and a query that partially reveals it. The hidden target is exactly L bits of unknown information under a uniform prior. Treat the DESIGN as the pair of query length L and query count R. Fix one candidate bitstring, set repeat count to R with seed_derivation sha256_index so that every repeat faces an independently drawn target, and record the score distribution.
