Under this design the number of matching positions is Binomial with parameters L and one half, so the mutual information between one observed score and the hidden target is computable directly from the observed distribution and can be compared against its analytic value, which is the entropy of that binomial, of order one half the logarithm of L, against a prior entropy of L bits. Sweep L over 8, 16, 32 and 64 with R equal to 200 (NEW DESIGN CHOICES). WHAT IT PRESERVES: information gain as the utility; a design, namely query length and query count, as the object judged; and the method's central distinction between the pre-experimental expectation, computed analytically, and the realised distribution, measured. It also preserves the saturation phenomenon, since information per query grows only logarithmically in L while the unknown grows linearly in L. WHAT IT LOSES: the prior is not user-supplied but fixed by construction to uniform over two-to-the-L targets; the likelihood is noiseless and therefore degenerate; and there is no way to misspecify the prior, so the robustness question, which is exactly the one the template already disclaims, remains untouchable. WHICH CLAIM: expected information gain per query for this one design family, and its saturation with L. It supports a calibration of the bench's own information geometry and a check that analytic and measured utility agree, which is a genuine instrument test. It supports no claim about any real study design.

QUESTION: Given only observational measurements of several variables, and no experiments, which pairs of variables could possibly be directly connected? The method rules connections out rather than establishing them.
MECHANISM: Start with the complete undirected graph, every pair joined. Then delete edges. For each remaining pair, test whether the two variables are independent given some set of the others, and test with conditioning sets in increasing order of size: first the empty set, which is plain marginal independence, then all single conditioning variables drawn from the neighbours of either endpoint, then all pairs, and so on up to the allowed maximum. The moment a conditioning set is found that makes the pair independent at the chosen significance level, delete that edge and record the separating set. When no more edges can be removed, the surviving graph is the skeleton. Orientation is a separate later phase that uses the recorded separating sets to find colliders and then propagates; this template stops before that. The whole method rests on assumptions the data cannot check: causal sufficiency, meaning no unmeasured common causes, plus faithfulness and the Markov condition.
CANDIDATE: The edge set, which starts complete and shrinks. What is judged is which edges survive.
WORLD: A dataset. The environment supplies a finite sample from some joint distribution, and its finiteness is the whole difficulty: every independence decision is a hypothesis test with error in both directions, and errors propagate, because the neighbour sets used for later tests depend on earlier deletions.
WHAT_CHANGES: The significance level alpha, the maximum conditioning set size, and, in any honest study, the sample and its seed.
MEASURED: The template asks for skeleton density, edges retained over edges possible, continuous between zero and one. Better statistics exist when a ground truth graph is available: structural Hamming distance to the true skeleton, or precision and recall over edges. All scalar.
INFORMATIVE_FAILURE: Informative in a specific and slightly awkward way. A skeleton that stays dense tells you the independence tests lacked power, which is a statement about sample size and not about causality. A skeleton that empties out tells you alpha was too permissive, or that many variables are near-deterministic functions of each other, which breaks faithfulness. Either way the failure diagnoses the INSTRUMENT rather than the world, and that is genuinely useful, because it forces the sample-size question to be settled before any causal claim is made. What a failure does not leave behind is any information about direction.
SOURCE_CHECK: VERIFIED - Spirtes, Glymour and Scheines, Causation, Prediction, and Search, MIT Press, is the standard reference for the PC algorithm and the second edition is 2000. The described adjacency-pruning phase, the increasing conditioning-set order, the separating sets and the causal sufficiency assumption are all as stated.
BLOCKER: R-BACKEND - mature implementations exist, causal-learn, pcalg and Tetrad among them, and the bench would only have to hand over a seed and parameters and fossilize one returned scalar. MEASUREMENT capability, and cheap. R-EXECUTOR - a self-contained kind that plants a graph, samples from a linear Gaussian structural equation model, runs the pruning phase and returns density or structural Hamming distance. Also MEASUREMENT. R-REPAIR - both parameters are null in param_space, so the template cannot be admitted as it stands on any route; that is a missing specification rather than a capability gap.
FAITHFUL: A faithful version needs a data object in the world, since PC consumes a sample and not a seed alone, and it needs the conditional independence test to be a real hypothesis test with a stated null. It also needs a planted ground-truth graph if the result is to be scored at all, because skeleton density on its own is uninterpretable without knowing the density of the truth.
REDUCTION: Plant the graph, run the real algorithm, return one number. Use a small planted directed acyclic graph, six nodes and seven edges as a NEW DESIGN CHOICE since the source values were destroyed, generate n samples from a linear Gaussian structural equation model seeded from the world seed, run the standard PC adjacency phase with Fisher-z tests, and return structural Hamming distance to the true skeleton as the single scalar. Propose alpha in the set 0.01, 0.05, 0.1 and maximum conditioning set size 2, both marked NEW DESIGN CHOICE. The part worth doing even before that executor exists: this template is an unusually good probe of the bench's own repeat semantics, and the design can be settled now. PC on a fixed sample is deterministic. Therefore under repeat.seed_derivation = constant with state = reset and count above one, every repeat is provably the identical computation and the bench should raise degenerate_by_construction. Under sha256_index each repeat is a DIFFERENT planted graph and a different sample, so the repeats measure a population of graphs rather than the sampling variability of one graph. Those are two different scientific questions and the template as written does not say which it wants. What a causal discovery researcher almost certainly wants is the third thing, the sampling distribution with the graph held fixed and only the sample advancing, and the current seed derivation CANNOT express it, because one integer seeds both the graph and the sample. That is a concrete and small substrate finding: the bench needs a way to hold one part of a world fixed while varying another. WHAT IT PRESERVES: the pruning mechanism intact, the alpha-versus-density tradeoff, and the finite-sample dependence that is the real content. WHAT IT LOSES: orientation, the completed partially directed acyclic graph, latent confounders and selection bias, all of which the template's own rationale already disclaims. WHICH CLAIM IT SUPPORTS: that skeleton recovery error is a function of sample size and alpha, measured rather than asserted, on a graph whose truth is known by construction.

QUESTION: When a new problem arrives, can a memory of past cases return the genuinely most similar past case, and does the choice of similarity measure change which case comes back?
MECHANISM: Case-based reasoning runs a four step cycle, retrieve, reuse, revise, retain. This template isolates the first step. A case base holds N past cases, each described by a vector of D features together with the solution that was used. A new problem arrives described in the same features. A similarity function scores every stored case against the query, either as plain geometric closeness, Euclidean or cosine, or with domain knowledge weighting some features more heavily than others. The cases are ranked and the top one is returned with its similarity score. In the full cycle that case's solution would then be adapted, tested and stored back, but none of that happens here.
CANDIDATE: The query case. What is judged is the retrieval, that is, the similarity score of the top ranked case, and in a stricter design whether the retrieved case's solution was in fact the right one.
WORLD: A case base of N points in a D dimensional feature space plus a similarity function. The environment supplies the memory, the geometry, and, if accuracy rather than raw similarity is being measured, the ground truth nearest neighbour.
WHAT_CHANGES: Case base size, feature dimensionality, similarity metric, and the query.
MEASURED: Top one similarity, continuous on 0 to 1. Optionally retrieval accuracy against a labelled correct neighbour, which is a different and much more meaningful number.
INFORMATIVE_FAILURE: Informative, but with a trap that has to be named. Top one similarity falls as D rises simply because distances concentrate in high dimension, so a failure at large D is the expected geometry and not a defect of any metric. What the failure leaves is the concentration curve itself, similarity against D at fixed N, which is exactly the useful object. The trap is that a threshold on raw similarity is close to always satisfied at low D and close to never satisfied at high D, so a rule frozen without first computing the attainable range can be degenerate before it runs. A failure of the reuse claim, by contrast, leaves nothing at all, because this template never touches reuse.
SOURCE_CHECK: VERIFIED. Aamodt and Plaza, Case-Based Reasoning: Foundational Issues, Methodological Variations, and System Approaches, AI Communications volume 7 number 1, 1994. That paper is the canonical statement of the retrieve, reuse, revise, retain cycle, and isolating the retrieve phase is a normal thing to do with it.
BLOCKER: R-EXECUTOR: a measurement capability. No existing kind computes a distance between two vectors. Note what is NOT blocking: the case base needs no persistent state, because it can be derived deterministically from the world seed exactly the way the bitstring target already is, so this is the cheapest kind of new executor, a pure function of seed and parameters. R-COMPOSE: an adjudication capability. Comparing three similarity metrics is a comparison across specs, and the outcome rule is one field, one operator, one value, so no spec can hold the contrast. It has to be computed downstream from three fossils. R-SUBSTRATE: a state capability. Feeding the retrieved case forward into reuse requires output to input chaining, which the bench does not have.
FAITHFUL: A faithful version needs a seeded case base generator, the three similarity functions implemented separately, and a labelled ground truth neighbour so that retrieval accuracy rather than raw similarity is the reported number. It also needs a second stage that adapts the retrieved solution and scores it, because without that the experiment measures the geometry of a synthetic point cloud and says nothing about reasoning.
REDUCTION: A surprisingly faithful reduction runs on the bench as it stands, because evaluate_bitstring already is a similarity oracle. Read the hidden target derived from the seed and the length as one stored case, the submitted bits as the query, and the returned score as Hamming similarity between them. Then case base size maps onto repeat count with seed_derivation sha256_index, since each repeat draws an independent hidden case, and the maximum score over the N repeats is precisely the top one retrieval similarity over a random case base. Feature dimensionality maps onto length. The maximum over repeats cannot be the outcome rule, because no aggregation across repeats is permitted, so the retrieval statistic is computed downstream, which makes this R-COMPOSE over specs that each run now. WHAT IT PRESERVES: the retrieval statistic itself, and, more valuable, its calibration. The expected top one Hamming similarity over N random cases of length L is the expectation of the maximum of N binomial draws divided by L, so the whole attainable range of the statistic is known in closed form before any threshold is frozen. It also preserves the concentration effect that makes high dimensional retrieval hard, because the spread of that maximum narrows as L grows. WHAT IT LOSES: the metric axis entirely, since Hamming is the only similarity the scorer can express, so euclidean, cosine and knowledge_guided are all unreachable; structured cases; labels; and the reuse, revise and retain steps that are the rest of the cycle. WHICH CLAIM: it supports a claim that top one similarity in a case base with no structure is a known function of base size and dimension, and therefore that any retrieval threshold chosen without that calibration is uninformative. That is a real methodological result about the field and it is reachable now. It supports no claim about any actual similarity metric. NEW DESIGN CHOICE, since two axes are null: case_base_size in 8, 64, 512 mapped to repeat count, feature_dimensions in 16, 32, 64, 128 mapped to length.

QUESTION: Can you prove a property about a system too big to check directly, by checking a deliberately blurred version of it and sharpening the blur only where the blur lies to you?
MECHANISM: Build a coarse abstraction of the system that keeps every real behaviour and also admits some fake ones, so it over-approximates. Ask a model checker whether the property holds on the abstraction. If yes, it holds on the real system too and you are done. If no, the checker hands back a counterexample trace. Replay that trace on the concrete system. If it reproduces, the bug is real and you are done. If it does not, it was an artifact of the blurring, and the trace tells you WHICH distinction the abstraction discarded; you add that distinction back, refine, and loop. The loop terminates because each refinement strictly splits the abstract state space.
CANDIDATE: The abstraction. What varies is which distinctions it keeps; what is judged is whether it is precise enough to settle the property.
WORLD: A concrete transition system plus a property to check. The world supplies a model checker, a concrete replay oracle, and, critically, counterexample traces rather than merely a yes or no.
WHAT_CHANGES: initial_abstraction_bits, either 11000000 or 11110000, and property_bits, 10101010. These parameter values survived ingest intact and are bitstrings of length eight, which strongly suggests an intended encoding onto the existing bitstring kind.
MEASURED: In the real method, a three-way outcome, property proven, real bug found, or refine again, together with the number of refinement rounds and the final abstraction size.
INFORMATIVE_FAILURE: Very informative. A refinement loop that fails to terminate within budget leaves the sequence of abstractions it tried, and that sequence directly measures how much the counterexample guidance is worth: a loop that removes one spurious distinction per round is being guided, a loop that thrashes is not. A spurious counterexample that cannot be diagnosed as spurious leaves a concrete, nameable gap in the replay oracle.
SOURCE_CHECK: VERIFIED. Clarke, Grumberg, Jha, Lu and Veith, Counterexample-Guided Abstraction Refinement, Computer Aided Verification 2000. The Clarke et al 2000 attribution is correct and the loop described is the method. Confirmed from established knowledge.
BLOCKER: R-COMPOSE, a measurement capability is missing and it is the decisive one, because evaluate_bitstring returns a SCALAR score and never the WITNESS, so a producer running the loop across specs learns how many positions disagree but never which, and CEGAR without the counterexample is not CEGAR, it is blind generate-and-test; R-EXECUTOR, the fix is small and specific, an executor or adapter that returns the disagreement mask alongside the score, which is a measurement capability; R-BACKEND, no capability is missing, an existing model checker could be invoked and its counterexample fossilized; R-SUBSTRATE, a control-flow capability is missing for any single-spec version, namely a bounded loop with output-to-input chaining, since refinement round N+1 must consume round N's trace and no payload may change inside a spec.
FAITHFUL: A faithful implementation needs a transition system, a property language, a model checker that emits traces, and a concrete simulator to adjudicate spuriousness. It needs a refinement operator that consumes a trace and returns a strictly finer abstraction, and the loop must be able to run to fixpoint rather than to a fixed count.
REDUCTION: A real and unusually clean reduction exists, and it yields a quantitative result about the method itself. Take the template's own numbers at face value, length 8, and treat the hidden target as the concrete behaviour. One spec is one refinement round: submit the current abstraction as bits and read score, the fraction of the eight positions on which the abstraction agrees with concrete behaviour. A score below 1.0 means a counterexample exists and the property is unsettled; solved true means it is settled. The producer holds the loop across specs, flipping bits to raise the score, starting from each of the two given abstractions. Now run two arms. Arm A is the bench as it stands, where the producer sees only the count of disagreements and must refine blind. Arm B is an oracle simulation, where the producer is separately told which position disagreed, imitating a real counterexample trace. Both arms run to score 1.0 or to a budget, over many seeds. WHAT IT PRESERVES: the abstraction as a candidate, monotone refinement toward a property, termination as the object of study, and rounds-to-proof as the measurable. WHAT IT LOSES: over-approximation semantics, because a Hamming score is symmetric and cannot distinguish a false alarm from a missed behaviour, so the spurious-versus-genuine adjudication, which is half of CEGAR, is simply absent. It also loses scale, and scale is the method's entire reason to exist. WHICH CLAIM: the gap between arm A and arm B measures, in rounds, what a counterexample witness is worth relative to a scalar oracle. For length L a witness-bearing loop should finish in at most L rounds while a count-only loop pays a real search cost. Measuring that gap on the current bench is a pre-registerable, evidence-backed argument for adding witness-returning executors, and it is the version worth running.

QUESTION: Can a synthesis loop that repeatedly proposes a program and gets back one concrete failing input find a correct program before it runs out of attempts, and how does that depend on how big the space of programs is?
MECHANISM: The programmer writes a sketch, a program with holes. The synthesizer solves an inductive query: find hole values that make the program correct on the current finite set of concrete example inputs. That candidate goes to a verifier, typically a SAT or SMT solver, which checks it against the full specification over all inputs. If verification fails the verifier returns a concrete counterexample input, which is added to the example set, and the loop repeats with a strictly harder inductive query. The loop ends when verification succeeds or the iteration budget is exhausted. The essential property is that each failure permanently narrows the next proposal, so the example set is a monotone accumulation of hardness.
CANDIDATE: The completed program, that is the vector of hole values. It is judged by a verifier that returns a verdict and a witness, not by a graded score.
WORLD: A full specification, a sketch or grammar bounded by sketch_size, and a finite input domain. The world's essential supply is the verifier, because the counterexample and not the pass or fail is what drives the method.
WHAT_CHANGES: max_iterations, unknown because the source destroyed the value. sketch_size, also unknown.
MEASURED: Solved or not solved as a boolean, iterations consumed as an integer, and the size and composition of the accumulated counterexample set.
INFORMATIVE_FAILURE: Very informative and directly reusable. A failed CEGIS run leaves the counterexample set, which is a compressed description of exactly what made the problem hard, is independent of the synthesizer that produced it, and can be replayed to warm-start a different synthesizer. Non-termination also localises: the holes that keep changing across iterations are the under-constrained ones. A failure here is closer to a deliverable than to a loss.
SOURCE_CHECK: PLAUSIBLE. Solar-Lezama's sketching work is real and is the standard origin of the CEGIS loop, and a 2008 Berkeley dissertation titled "Program Synthesis by Sketching" is the usual citation, but the web search budget was exhausted this session so the exact 2008 attribution could not be confirmed. Note that the CEGIS loop itself is often traced to the earlier Solar-Lezama et al. sketching paper rather than to the dissertation.
BLOCKER: R-COMPOSE: missing state. The producer can hold the loop, but each spec's counterexample must become the next spec's payload, and output-to-input chaining across specs is a substrate capability the bench does not offer. R-BACKEND: missing executor and missing measurement. There is no adapter that hands a formula to an external SAT or SMT solver, and no result field can carry a counterexample, which is a structured witness rather than a scalar. R-SUBSTRATE: missing control flow. An iterate-until-verified loop with a growing example set cannot exist inside a sealed spec whose payload is fixed for its whole life. R-EXECUTOR: missing adjudication. A verifier that decides a universally quantified property is not a scorer; the bench has scoring but no adjudication over a quantifier.
FAITHFUL: A program grammar with typed holes, an inductive synthesizer over a finite example set, an external verifier that returns a concrete witness on failure, and a loop with a monotonically growing example set. The spec must be able to carry a set-valued input, the example set, and to return a witness-valued output, and the outcome must be able to report iterations-to-success rather than one scalar comparison.
REDUCTION: A concrete and surprisingly faithful CEGIS runs on the existing scorer. The program is a candidate bitstring of length L, the holes are its L bits, and sketch_size maps directly to L. The specification is the hidden target. The bench does not hand back a counterexample, but one can be manufactured from scores: the producer submits a candidate, then submits the candidate with bit i flipped; if the score rises, position i is a concrete counterexample, a specific place where the program is wrong. That is a real discriminating witness and it drives a real inductive step, because a confirmed bit is permanently fixed and the next proposal is drawn from a strictly smaller space. Budget equals number of specs, playing max_iterations. PRESERVES: the loop structure, the property that each failure narrows the next proposal, the monotone accumulation of confirmed constraints, the iteration budget as the outcome axis, and the sketch-size scaling. LOSES: logic and the SAT query, universal quantification, since the specification here is a single point so verification degenerates to equality, and the exponential blowup of the inductive step, which is the reason CEGIS is interesting. CLAIM SUPPORTED: how iterations-to-solve scales with the number of holes under a one-bit counterexample oracle, and whether a smarter probe policy beats naive left-to-right probing. Both curves are pre-registrable and falsifiable, and the naive baseline has a known form near L probes, which makes this double as a calibration of the harness. HONEST CEILING: this reproduces CEGIS's control flow without CEGIS's hardness, so it can support claims about loop efficiency and about the harness, and no claim at all about synthesis. NEW DESIGN CHOICE: L in 8, 16, 32, 64; max_iterations equal to four times L.

QUESTION: Does making the test cases evolve against the solutions, instead of holding them fixed, keep a search from getting stuck on a local optimum?
MECHANISM: Two populations are maintained at once. Hosts are candidate solutions, in Hillis's case sorting networks. Parasites are sets of test cases, in that case lists to be sorted. Host fitness is how many of the co-located parasite's cases it handles correctly; parasite fitness is how many it makes the host fail. Both populations reproduce with variation on a spatial grid, so a host that is good only against the currently common cases is immediately punished when the parasites shift. The difficulty of the test set is therefore a moving function of current host competence, which is what prevents the search from converging on a static benchmark it has memorised.
CANDIDATE: Two candidates at once, and that is the point. The host varies in its solution structure; the parasite varies in which test cases it presents. Each is judged only against the other, so neither has an absolute fitness.
WORLD: A shared spatial arena holding both populations, with locality so that hosts meet nearby parasites. The world supplies the interaction rule that turns a host-parasite meeting into a pair of fitnesses, and nothing more; there is no external objective.
WHAT_CHANGES: Host population size and parasite population size, both offered as 50, 100 or 200. Implicitly also the generation count and the mutation operators, neither of which is in the param_space.
MEASURED: Host performance over generations, and in the honest version the quality of the final host against an independent held-out test set rather than against the surviving parasites. The scale is a fraction of test cases passed.
INFORMATIVE_FAILURE: Genuinely informative, and this method's failures are famous. Disengagement, where parasites become so hard or so easy that fitness carries no gradient, is diagnostic and visible in the fitness variance. Cycling, where hosts and parasites chase each other around a loop forever, is the classic Red Queen failure and leaves a recoverable period. Both failures leave a full trajectory of two coupled populations, which is data about the coupling even when no good host emerges.
SOURCE_CHECK: VERIFIED. Hillis 1990, Co-evolving parasites improve simulated evolution as an optimization procedure, Physica D volume 42, is a foundational and correctly attributed paper on coevolving sorting networks with test-case parasites. Confirmed from established literature knowledge; the web search budget was exhausted before this template, but the attribution is not in doubt.
BLOCKER: R-WORLD is blocked on state, specifically the absence of any second organism type and of a population at all, since one spec has one world holding one integer and no notion of an opponent; R-COMPOSE is blocked on adjudication, because relative fitness is inherently a two-field comparison, host score against parasite score, and the outcome rule permits exactly one field and one operator; R-EXECUTOR is blocked on state again, since even a new kind would need to carry two populations across generations, which is output-to-input chaining and therefore really an R-SUBSTRATE request wearing an executor costume.
FAITHFUL: A faithful implementation needs two typed populations with heredity and variation, an interaction rule that computes both fitnesses from a single meeting, and generational chaining so that the output population of one step is the input population of the next. It also needs an independent held-out evaluation set, because measuring the final host against the final parasites is exactly the control that memory says is drawn from the treatment's own selection relation and is therefore not a control at all.
REDUCTION: One survives, at the producer layer, and it is more faithful than it first appears. The parasite population becomes the SEED POOL, since the seed is what determines the hidden target and therefore the difficulty. Run two arms across specs with the same candidate-improvement procedure. In the iid arm the producer draws each next seed uniformly. In the adversarial arm the producer picks each next seed from the set on which the current best candidate scored WORST, which is precisely parasite selection: the test is selected for host failure. Measure candidate score improvement per spec in each arm, downstream. WHAT IT PRESERVES: the defining coupling, that test difficulty is a function of current host competence, plus the host and test asymmetry, the arms-race dynamic across generations, and a clean iid control that is not drawn from the adversarial selection relation. WHAT IT LOSES: the parasites have no genotype and no heredity, so they cannot ACCUMULATE structure across generations and cannot invent a new kind of hard case; they can only be filtered from a fixed pool. That makes this adversarial sampling, which is the one-sided half of coevolution, and it cannot exhibit Red Queen cycling because only one side has memory. WHICH CLAIM IT SUPPORTS: that adversarially selected test seeds slow measured candidate improvement relative to iid seeds, and that a candidate tuned on adversarial seeds does or does not transfer to held-out iid seeds. That is a real and testable coevolution claim, and it needs no bench change at all.

QUESTION: When two scientific theories compete over the same body of evidence, can the choice between them be reproduced by a simple mechanical process that only balances which theory explains more and contradicts less?
MECHANISM: Every proposition, whether hypothesis or evidence, becomes a unit in a network. If one hypothesis, possibly together with others, explains a proposition, symmetric excitatory links are created among all of them, with the weight divided among co-hypotheses so that explaining something with fewer assumptions pays better. If two propositions contradict, an inhibitory link is created. Evidence units also receive an excitatory link from a special always-on data unit, which is how observation gets its privileged pull. Activation is then updated in parallel over many cycles by a standard connectionist rule until activations stop changing. Units settling positive are accepted, units settling negative are rejected. The whole thing is parallel constraint satisfaction with no search and no explicit inference rules.
CANDIDATE: A hypothesis unit. What varies is its final activation, and what is judged is whether it is accepted, which depends on the whole network rather than on the unit alone.
WORLD: A hand-encoded corpus of propositions and explanatory relations, for example Lavoisier's oxygen case against phlogiston, or Darwin against special creation. The world supplies the network topology, and it is worth stating plainly that the encoding is the analyst's, which is where most of the method's leverage and most of its criticism both live.
WHAT_CHANGES: The number of hypothesis units, the number of evidence units and the number of update cycles allowed.
MEASURED: A settled activation per unit, continuous and bounded between minus one and one, plus whether the network settled at all within the cycle budget.
INFORMATIVE_FAILURE: A network that does not settle, or that accepts both ends of an inhibitory link, is a concrete artefact: you keep the exact link structure that produced the degeneracy and it becomes a permanent hard case for any future coherence model. Better still, a run whose accepted set FLIPS when the cycle budget is raised proves the reported result was never a fixed point, which falsifies that run's use as an adjudicator without any philosophical argument at all.
SOURCE_CHECK: VERIFIED. Thagard, Explanatory Coherence, Behavioral and Brain Sciences 12 (1989), pages 435 to 467, presents the seven principles and the connectionist implementation named ECHO, encoding coherence and incoherence as excitatory and inhibitory links and treating hypothesis evaluation as constraint satisfaction, applied to Lavoisier and to Darwin. The template's three axes, hypotheses, evidence and cycles, correspond to real dimensions of the model.
BLOCKER: R-EXECUTOR is missing both a measurement capability and a control-flow capability: the payload schema cannot carry a graph, and there is no fixed-point iteration anywhere in the bench, the only loop being the fixed step count of the random walk, which has no attractor. R-COMPOSE is missing an adjudication capability, because the interesting verdict is an ORDERING over hypothesis activations and the outcome rule forbids any ordering or two-field test. R-BACKEND is missing an execution-backend capability, though the executor here is small enough that the backend route is probably the wrong one.
FAITHFUL: A faithful version is a small executor, on the order of a hundred lines, taking a proposition list and a relation list as payload, building the weight matrix, running the update rule to convergence or to a declared cycle cap, and returning per-unit activations plus a settled flag. It needs no persistent state and no population. What it does need that the bench lacks is a payload able to carry structured input, and an outcome rule able to compare two activations, since accepted-over-its-rival is intrinsically a two-field question.
REDUCTION: Marginal, and it must be labelled a control rather than an instance. The one component of ECHO the current bench can genuinely exercise is the BUDGET-TRUNCATION HAZARD, the risk of reading a verdict off an iterative process that has not converged. Use random_walk_v0 with repeat state persist and seed_derivation linear_index, and run the same configuration at a small cycle budget and a large one, for instance steps of 50 against steps of 5000 at fixed step_scale, over 5 seeds (NEW DESIGN CHOICES; 5 seeds because a single seed cannot support a variance claim). Apply the same displacement threshold at both budgets and record how often the two budgets disagree. WHAT IT PRESERVES: only that a verdict read from an unconverged iterative process is a function of the budget, and that the fossil must therefore record the budget beside the verdict. WHAT IT LOSES: coherence, explanation, inhibition, competition between rival hypotheses, and, decisively, convergence itself, since ECHO settles to a fixed point whereas a random walk is a martingale that never settles. The reduction therefore yields an UPPER BOUND on truncation instability, not a model of ECHO. WHICH CLAIM: a methodological one only, that verdicts read at cycle budget C are budget-sensitive and here is the magnitude for a maximally unstable process. It supports nothing in philosophy of science. Anyone wanting the actual template should write the hundred-line executor instead; this reduction is honest but thin, and calling it an ECHO experiment would be a gesture.

QUESTION: Can a small set of mechanical rules, given nothing but a table of numbers, rediscover a quantitative law of nature such as the relation between a planet's distance from the sun and the time it takes to orbit?
MECHANISM: The system holds a table of observations with one column per measured variable and applies a very small set of data-driven heuristics in a loop. If a term is constant across the rows within tolerance, record it as a law and stop. If two terms increase together, define a new column that is their ratio. If one increases as the other decreases, define a new column that is their product. Then look again at the enlarged table for a constant term. Applied to distance D and period P, the recursion builds D over P, then that over P again, then a ratio of those, and arrives at D cubed over P squared being constant, which is Kepler's third law. Later versions add symmetry and common-divisor heuristics and intrinsic properties, and handle several independent variables by holding all but one fixed and sweeping. The essential point is that this is a search over DERIVED TERMS, not a fit of a pre-chosen functional form.
CANDIDATE: A derived term, an expression built from the measured columns. What is judged is whether that term is constant across rows.
WORLD: A clean data table. In the classical demonstrations the data are noiseless historical measurements and the world supplies exactly the variables the law needs and no distractors. That is the great weakness of the demonstration and everyone in the field knows it.
WHAT_CHANGES: The number of variables in the table and the noise level added to them. Both are null in this template and must be set.
MEASURED: Whether a constant term was found; the coefficient of variation of the best term, a continuous non-negative number; and the number of search steps taken to reach it, a count.
INFORMATIVE_FAILURE: Yes, and this is the most scientifically interesting part of the template. BACON's failure modes are why the field moved on. Under noise the constancy test either never fires, so nothing is found, or fires on a spurious term, so a false law is reported. The false-positive case is the valuable one: it measures how much noise the constancy tolerance will absorb before the method starts manufacturing laws, and that number is a property of the method, transferable to every descendant symbolic-regression system. A failure here leaves behind a calibrated false-discovery rate, which is more useful than one more successful rediscovery of Kepler.
SOURCE_CHECK: VERIFIED - the BACON series by Pat Langley with Herbert Simon and colleagues, running through the late 1970s and the 1980s and consolidated in Scientific Discovery: Computational Explorations of the Creative Processes, is real, and the rediscovery of Kepler's third law is one of its canonical demonstrations. The stated span 1978 to 1987 is consistent with the BACON.1 through BACON.5 sequence. Caveat on the noise axis: the early BACON systems were notably NOT noise tolerant, and noise handling is a later and partial addition, so an axis that sweeps noise is sweeping the system's known weak point rather than a designed parameter.
BLOCKER: R-COMPOSE - the bench forbids search inside a spec and BACON is nothing but search, so the recursion must live in the producer with each spec supplying one data point. CONTROL FLOW, specifically that repeat N plus one cannot depend on the result of repeat N. R-EXECUTOR - a self-contained kind that plants a law, generates a table, runs the heuristic recursion and returns one scalar. MEASUREMENT capability. R-REPAIR - variables and noise are both null and must be set before admission; a specification gap, not a capability gap.
FAITHFUL: A faithful version needs a data table in the world rather than a seed, a symbolic term representation the executor can extend, and an unbounded inner loop, since the number of recursion steps is not known in advance. It also needs the planted law to be known, so that a discovered term can be scored as right or wrong rather than merely constant.
REDUCTION: Two, and the second is the one I would actually run. First, the obvious one: a bacon_terms_v0 executor. Plant P equals k times D raised to the power 1.5, generate a table of rows with Gaussian noise at sigma, run the ratio-and-product recursion to a bounded depth, and return the coefficient of variation of the best constant term found. One scalar, one comparison, fits the outcome rule exactly. As NEW DESIGN CHOICES propose two variables and noise sigma in the set 0, 0.01, 0.05. Second, and this needs no new executor at all. evaluate_bitstring exposes a deterministic black-box function from a candidate to a continuous score between zero and one. A producer can run BACON's own recursion ACROSS specs: encode an integer as a bitstring and call that the independent variable, take the returned score as the dependent variable, build the table across many specs, and apply the ratio-product-constancy heuristics downstream. Here is why that is not a toy. The hidden target is derived by hashing, so it is KNOWN BY CONSTRUCTION that no smooth law relates the encoded integer to the score. Running BACON there therefore measures exactly one thing: how often BACON reports a law where none can exist, as a function of table size and constancy tolerance. That is a calibrated false-positive rate for the method, obtained for free, on a null that is not merely shuffled but structurally guaranteed. It answers directly the caveat the template's own rationale raises about what a SURVIVED verdict would and would not license. WHAT IT PRESERVES: the exact search heuristics, the constancy tolerance, and the dependence of discovery on table size. WHAT IT LOSES: the planted law, and therefore any true-positive rate. It is a one-sided measurement, and one-sided is the correct posture here: it can only ever produce evidence that the method over-reports. WHICH CLAIM IT SUPPORTS: a false-discovery-rate claim about heuristic induction, pinned to a landscape where the true answer is provably no law. Pair it later with the planted-law executor to get the other side.

QUESTION: Over a fixed number of steps, how far does an unbiased one dimensional random walk wander, and does the accumulated displacement stay inside the bounds that theory predicts?
MECHANISM: Start at the origin. Repeat a fixed number of times: draw a value uniformly from minus one to plus one, multiply by the step scale, add it to the current position. Report the final position and the displacement from the start. Because each increment is independent with mean zero and variance equal to the square of the step scale divided by three, the displacement after n steps is asymptotically normal with mean zero and standard deviation equal to the step scale times the square root of n over three. The characteristic prediction of the model is not any single endpoint but that the spread grows as the square root of the number of steps, which is the diffusive scaling law.
CANDIDATE: The realised trajectory, judged by its endpoint. Nothing is being optimised.
WORLD: A single integer seed feeding a pseudorandom generator, plus a step scale. The environment supplies only randomness and a length scale, which is why this is the one template in the chunk whose world is genuinely the bench's world.
WHAT_CHANGES: Number of steps, step scale, the derived seed per repeat, and whether state is reset or persisted between repeats.
MEASURED: Position and displacement, continuous and unbounded, in units of the step scale. The executor also returns start position, steps and step scale, so the fossil is self describing.
INFORMATIVE_FAILURE: Modest but real, and it points inwards rather than outwards. A displacement outside the predicted band is not a statement about diffusion, it is a statement about the bench's own pseudorandom source or about the step distribution, so a failure is a calibration finding on the instrument. Repeated over many seeds it becomes a usable test of uniformity and independence of the generator, which every other stochastic template on the bench silently depends on. A single walk that lands outside the band leaves nothing at all, because one endpoint is one draw from a wide distribution, and that is the main way this template can be run badly.
SOURCE_CHECK: PLAUSIBLE. The one dimensional discrete random walk with uniform increments is canonical and uncontroversial, and the diffusive scaling result is textbook. The template names no specific text, author or year, only standard discrete stochastic modelling texts, so there is no particular attribution available to confirm or refute. The method is real; there is simply nothing here to verify against.
BLOCKER: R-REPAIR: missing parameters, which is a spec completeness problem rather than a capability gap. Both steps and step_scale are null in the param space, and no executor may default a parameter, so the spec is rejected as written. Choosing numbers makes it R-NOW. R-NOW: nothing, once repaired. This is one of only two templates in the chunk that the bench can execute at all. R-COMPOSE: an adjudication capability. Every claim worth making here, that mean displacement is zero, that the standard deviation matches the step scale times the square root of n over three, that the spread doubles when the step count quadruples, is an aggregate over repeats or over specs. The outcome rule is one scalar comparison with no aggregation and no trend test, so the statistics must be computed downstream from the fossilized per repeat displacements.
FAITHFUL: A faithful version is an ensemble, not a run. It needs many independent seeds per cell of the step count and step scale grid, downstream estimation of the mean and variance of displacement, and a sweep over step counts so that the square root law is checked rather than assumed. It also needs the increment distribution and the generator to be documented, so that the predicted band is derived in advance rather than fitted after the fact.
REDUCTION: This template is already at the bench, so the useful work is not shrinking it but making it non vacuous, and there is a good design available. NEW DESIGN CHOICE, since both axes are null: step_scale fixed at 1.0, steps on a geometric ladder of 100, 400, 1600 and 6400 so that the predicted spread should double at each rung, repeat count 200 with seed_derivation sha256_index and state reset. The sha256_index choice is not cosmetic: with constant derivation, a stateless kind and state reset and a count above one, the bench flags degenerate_by_construction, and every repeat would be the identical computation. The per spec outcome rule is a per repeat containment check, absolute displacement no greater than three times the step scale times the square root of steps over three. Its expected violation rate is about three in a thousand, so both the attainable range and the eligible outcome are known before the rule is frozen, which is the whole point of choosing it this way. Downstream, fit the observed spread against the square root of the step count across the four rungs. WHAT IT PRESERVES: diffusive scaling, which is the only real content of the method, and the containment band, which is the only honest single scalar the method can produce. WHAT IT LOSES: any claim about physical Brownian motion, about drift, about first passage times, or about the generator being a good model of anything outside itself. WHICH CLAIM: that the bench's own random source produces diffusive scaling with the predicted constant. That is an instrument calibration result the rest of the bench can lean on, which makes this the highest value per unit effort template in the chunk. Worth adding as a second arm: run the same ladder with state persist, so that a long walk is taken in chunks, and check that the chunked walk composes into a single walk with the same law. That is a direct test of the only stateful path in the substrate, and nothing else in the inbox tests it.

QUESTION: How often does an aimless, undirected process stumble into something a standing criterion would call valuable?
MECHANISM: The account this template draws on breaks a serendipitous discovery into four parts. A prepared mind holds standing interests and evaluation criteria. A serendipity trigger occurs, and it is unsought, accidental and independent of what the agent was doing. A bridge is then constructed by the agent, connecting the trigger to something it cares about. A result follows, and the result must have value. The account grades an episode along three dimensions: chance, how unlikely and unsought the trigger was; sagacity, how much insight the bridge took; and value, how good the result is. Only the combination is serendipity.
CANDIDATE: A trajectory of an unguided stochastic process. What varies is where the wander goes; what is judged is whether it reaches a state a preset criterion calls valuable.
WORLD: A one-dimensional line with a fixed origin and a value threshold placed at some distance from it. The world supplies randomness and the threshold, and nothing else.
WHAT_CHANGES: steps and step_scale. Both parameter value sets were destroyed in ingest and are unknown; the axis names are real.
MEASURED: The signed final position and the displacement from the start, both continuous, compared once against a threshold.
INFORMATIVE_FAILURE: Moderately informative and in one specific way very much so. A run in which no threshold is ever crossed still supplies the base rate of accidental threshold crossing at a given steps and step_scale, and that base rate is the null that every other discovery claim on this bench should be scored against. What a failure leaves nothing of is the serendipity question itself, because nothing here can tell a lucky crossing apart from a perceptive one.
SOURCE_CHECK: VERIFIED, with a correction to the description. The work is Pease, Colton, Ramezani, Charnley and Reed, A Discussion on Serendipity in Creative Systems, Proceedings of the Fourth International Conference on Computational Creativity, ICCC 2013, pages 64 to 71. It does define the prepared mind, the serendipity trigger, the bridge and the result, and the three dimensions of chance, sagacity and value. It is a discussion paper proposing those dimensions, not a standards document, and it has five authors rather than the two named. Checked this session.
BLOCKER: R-REPAIR, the missing thing is parameter values, since steps and step_scale both arrived null and no executor may default a parameter, so the spec is rejected until an operator sets them; that is the only thing standing between this template and execution; R-COMPOSE, an adjudication capability is missing for the actual construct, since chance is measurable here but sagacity and the bridge are not, and no downstream analysis of position values can recover them.
FAITHFUL: A faithful implementation needs an agent with standing interests that were formed before the trigger, a mechanism that can notice an event it was not looking for, and a bridge operator that connects that event to an unrelated goal. It also needs the value criterion to be capable of being met by something not on the agent's current agenda, which is the exact property a pre-registered scalar threshold destroys.
REDUCTION: A reduction exists, it is nearly free, and its honest scope is narrow. Set steps to 200 and step_scale to 0.1, both NEW DESIGN CHOICES, and set the outcome rule to displacement greater than or equal to 2.0 mapping to SURVIVED. Use repeat count 200 with seed_derivation sha256_index and state reset, so the 200 repeats are independent walks. The crossing frequency is a calibrated base rate of accidental value. Sweep steps and step_scale across specs to get the rate as a surface. One trap must be flagged: the bench's degenerate_by_construction check fires only for a constant seed meeting a STATELESS kind, and random_walk_v0 is stateful, so a constant seed with state reset and count greater than 1 gives 200 byte-identical walks and will NOT be flagged. That configuration must be avoided by hand. WHAT IT PRESERVES: the chance dimension exactly, an unguided process with no objective, and the prepared mind in its thinnest possible form, since a pre-registered outcome rule is literally a criterion fixed before the trigger. WHAT IT LOSES: sagacity and the bridge, wholly. Nothing recognises an unsought result, nothing connects it to an unrelated goal, and a criterion fixed in advance means the agent was in fact looking for exactly this, which is the precise negation of serendipity. WHICH CLAIM: only the base rate of luck at a given budget. That is not serendipity and must never be written up as such, but it is the correct denominator for every serendipity claim the bench later makes, and no other template in this chunk supplies it.

QUESTION: Can a search driven only by how different a behaviour is from everything already seen keep producing new behaviours indefinitely, with no goal and no fitness function telling it what counts as better?
MECHANISM: Each individual is run in a domain and reduced to a behaviour characterisation, a low-dimensional vector such as a final position. Its novelty is the mean distance to its k nearest neighbours among the current population together with an archive of previously encountered behaviours. Selection is on novelty alone. Individuals that are sufficiently novel are inserted into the archive, which makes that region of behaviour space less rewarding for everything that comes after, so the search is continuously pushed outward. The archive is the mechanism: without it the search forgets and cycles.
CANDIDATE: An individual, that is a genome mapped to a controller. It is judged only by the distance of its behaviour from stored behaviours, and crucially the comparison is on behaviour, not genome, so two very different genomes with the same behaviour are interchangeable.
WORLD: A domain that maps a genome to a behaviour vector, plus the archive. The archive is properly part of the world here, and it is non-stationary: the same individual has a different novelty score at different times, which is what makes this method impossible to express as a fixed fitness landscape.
WHAT_CHANGES: archive_size, unknown because the source destroyed the value. k_nearest, also unknown. Plus the population across generations.
MEASURED: Novelty score, a continuous non-negative distance, along with archive growth rate and behaviour-space coverage over time.
INFORMATIVE_FAILURE: Informative and diagnostic. If the search stalls, the archive plus the insertion times remain, and from them you can distinguish the two failure causes that matter: the behaviour descriptor is degenerate, visible as an archive that saturates inside a small region, or the genotype-to-phenotype map is degenerate, visible as many distinct genomes collapsing onto the same behaviour. Separating a bad descriptor from a bad generator is the central open question in this area, so a stall is a real measurement.
SOURCE_CHECK: VERIFIED. Confirmed in DBLP: Joel Lehman and Kenneth O. Stanley, "Exploiting Open-Endedness to Solve Problems Through the Search for Novelty", ALIFE 2008, pages 329 to 336.
BLOCKER: R-COMPOSE: missing adjudication. The archive and the k-nearest-neighbour distance can live in the producer, but novelty is defined relative to other specs' results, and the outcome rule cannot express a value computed from anything other than this spec's own fields. R-SUBSTRATE: missing state. An archive that persists across evaluations and changes the score of later evaluations is precisely the mutable shared state the sealed one-world model excludes. R-REPAIR: archive_size and k_nearest are null and must be chosen before anything runs. R-EXECUTOR: missing measurement, but only mildly; random_walk_v0 already returns an endpoint, which is a legitimate one-dimensional behaviour characterisation.
FAITHFUL: A behaviour characterisation function over a genome, a persistent archive with an explicit insertion policy, a k-nearest-neighbour distance over that archive, and generational selection and variation over a population. That is a population plus mutable shared state, and both are excluded by one world per spec.
REDUCTION: This is one of the strongest reductions in the chunk, because random_walk_v0 already is a behaviour characterisation function. The genome is the triple of seed_root, steps and step_scale; the behaviour is displacement, a one-dimensional descriptor. The producer runs a batch of walk specs, reads displacements, and holds the archive downstream. Novelty of a candidate equals the mean absolute displacement difference to its k nearest archive entries; the top-novelty genomes are selected and mutated by perturbing seed_root and jittering step_scale to form the next batch; sufficiently novel behaviours are inserted into a bounded archive. That is real novelty search, not a gesture: the archive genuinely feeds back and genuinely changes later scores. PRESERVES: behaviour-based rather than fitness-based selection, the archive feedback that devalues visited regions, archive_size and k_nearest as live knobs, and the divergence-versus-stall question with its diagnostic. LOSES: high-dimensional behaviour space, and, more seriously, deception. A smooth monotone genome-to-displacement map has no dead ends, and beating an objective on a deceptive task is novelty search's headline result, so that claim is out of reach. CLAIM SUPPORTED: how archive_size and k affect coverage rate and stall time of a divergent search in a bounded descriptor space. PRE-REGISTERED NULL, and it is the likely outcome: in one dimension with a smooth map, novelty search should be beaten by uniform sampling of seeds, and confirming that is a clean, useful kill rather than a disappointment. To make deception reachable at all, the descriptor must be made non-monotone in the genome, for example by having the producer fold step_scale through a multimodal function of the genome before submitting the spec. NEW DESIGN CHOICE: archive_size 250, k_nearest 15, batch 100, 40 generations, steps 200.

QUESTION: In an environment too large to count visits to individual states, can a learned density model stand in for a visit counter well enough to tell an agent which parts of the world it has not really seen?
MECHANISM: A sequential density model is fit online over observed states. For a state just seen, the model gives a probability before the update and a probability after being trained on that one observation. The increase, called the prediction gain, is large for a state the model finds surprising and small for one it already expects. From those two probabilities a pseudo-count is derived algebraically, and it behaves like an empirical visit count while being defined for states never visited. An exploration bonus proportional to one over the square root of the pseudo-count is added to the reward, and the agent's policy then pursues that bonus, which is what drives it into unvisited regions.
CANDIDATE: The agent's policy, judged by where it goes. What varies is the density model class and the bonus scale, and downstream of those, the states the agent chooses to visit.
WORLD: A sequential decision environment with high-dimensional observations, sparse or absent extrinsic reward, and a large enough state space that tabular counting is impossible. The world supplies observations, a transition rule responding to actions, and reward.
WHAT_CHANGES: The density model, offered as CTS or PixelCNN, and the bonus scale, whose range arrived null.
MEASURED: State coverage and extrinsic return over training, plus the agreement between pseudo-counts and true counts where true counts happen to be known. Coverage is a count, return is unbounded, agreement is a ratio.
INFORMATIVE_FAILURE: Mixed. A failed exploration run leaves a visitation histogram, which is directly informative about where the bonus dried up and therefore about which states the density model considered familiar too early. That is concrete and reusable. What it does not leave is any separation between two very different causes, a bad density model and a bad policy optimiser, so a bare failure is not attributable without the estimator being measured separately.
SOURCE_CHECK: VERIFIED with a caveat. Bellemare, Srinivasan, Ostrovski, Schaul, Saxton and Munos, Unifying Count-Based Exploration and Intrinsic Motivation, NeurIPS 2016, introduces pseudo-counts from a CTS density model and the one over root pseudo-count bonus. The PixelCNN option in the param_space belongs to the 2017 follow-up by Ostrovski and colleagues, count-based exploration with neural density models, not to the cited paper, so one of the two axis values is attributed to the wrong publication. Confirmed from established literature knowledge; the search budget was exhausted before this template.
BLOCKER: R-SUBSTRATE is blocked on control flow, and this is the deep one: an exploration bonus is only exploration if it CHANGES THE NEXT ACTION, which requires output-to-input chaining within a run, and the payload of a sealed spec is fixed for the whole spec by construction; R-COMPOSE is blocked on a measurement, since to fit any density model downstream the bench must emit the per-step state trace and random_walk_v0 returns only the final position and displacement, not the intermediate states; R-BACKEND is blocked on the same missing trace, plus the absence of any action space for an external RL library to act in.
FAITHFUL: A faithful implementation needs an environment with actions and observations, a policy that can be updated during a run, an online density model over observations, and a reward channel the bonus can be added to. The bench would have to allow a run to be a training loop rather than a single measurement, which is a substrate change and not an executor change.
REDUCTION: A real one exists, and it works by deleting the agent and keeping the estimator. The theoretical core of the paper is that pseudo-counts approximate true visit counts, and that claim can be tested with no policy at all. Run random_walk_v0 with repeat state persist so the repeats form ONE trajectory, sweeping the number of repeats to get streams of increasing length. Bin position onto a fixed grid, which makes true visit counts exactly known. Downstream, fit a sequential density model over the bin sequence, compute the prediction gain and pseudo-count for each observation, and compare pseudo-count against the true running count. NEW DESIGN CHOICE, since bonus_scale arrived null: steps 1, step_scale 1.0, 5000 persisted repeats, bin width 1.0, and the bonus scale is not needed at all because no bonus is consumed. WHAT IT PRESERVES: the density model, the prediction gain, the pseudo-count derivation, and a ground-truth count to check it against, which is exactly the paper's central technical claim. WHAT IT LOSES: the entire agentic half. No actions, no policy, no reward, no bonus feedback, so nothing here is exploration. It also loses the hard part of the problem, because a 1-D binned walk is nearly tabular and the whole motivation was non-tabular state spaces, so success here is necessary and very far from sufficient. WHICH CLAIM IT SUPPORTS: that a given pseudo-count estimator is consistent on a stream with known counts. That is instrument calibration and must not be reported as an exploration result. IMPORTANT PREREQUISITE: even this needs random_walk_v0 to expose the per-step positions, or the walk must be run with steps equal to 1 so that each repeat contributes exactly one observable position, which is the trick that makes the reduction possible today.

QUESTION: Given that you can only afford a fixed number of measurements, where should you put them so that the model you intend to fit comes out as sharply determined as possible?
MECHANISM: Fix a model, for example a polynomial of a chosen degree, and fix the region over which measurements may be taken. A design is a specific list of measurement locations. Build the model matrix whose rows are the model's basis functions evaluated at those locations, and form the information matrix as its transpose times itself. The volume of the resulting confidence ellipsoid for the fitted coefficients shrinks as the determinant of that matrix grows, so the determinant, usually scaled by the number of parameters and expressed as an efficiency between zero and one, is the design's score. Exchange algorithms improve a design by repeatedly swapping one measurement location for another and keeping the swap if the determinant rises.
CANDIDATE: An exact design, that is, a particular set of n measurement locations. It is judged by the determinant of its information matrix, or equivalently by its D-efficiency relative to the theoretical continuous optimum.
WORLD: The assumed model and the design region. The world supplies the regression basis and the boundaries within which measurements may be placed. No data is generated and no responses are observed; the criterion depends only on where you would measure, not on what you would find.
WHAT_CHANGES: The number of design points and the polynomial degree.
MEASURED: The determinant of the information matrix, or the D-efficiency in the range zero to one; a single continuous number per design.
INFORMATIVE_FAILURE: A design whose determinant is zero is not a null result, it is a proof: the design is singular and at least one model coefficient is not estimable from it at all. The failure leaves the rank deficiency and hence exactly which parameter combination is inestimable and why, whether because there are fewer support points than parameters or because support points coincide. That is reusable and it also protects downstream work, since fitting a model on a singular design produces confident nonsense.
SOURCE_CHECK: VERIFIED. Atkinson and Donev, Optimum Experimental Designs, Clarendon Press, Oxford, 1992, Oxford Statistical Science Series volume 8, is the standard monograph; it contains chapters on D-optimum designs and on algorithms for constructing exact D-optimum designs, and design size and polynomial degree are its own working axes.
BLOCKER: R-EXECUTOR is missing a measurement capability and nothing else: no executor accepts a list of design points and a model degree as payload, and none returns a determinant. There is no state gap, no control-flow gap and no adjudication gap whatever, because d_efficiency at least 0.95 is already precisely one field, one operator, one value. This is the single cheapest template in the chunk, blocked by one missing measurement. R-BACKEND is missing an execution-backend capability, an adapter to an existing optimal design library, but the calculation is small enough that the adapter would cost more than the executor.
FAITHFUL: A faithful version is roughly thirty lines: accept a point list and a degree, build the model matrix, compute the scaled determinant, return d_efficiency together with the matrix rank so that the singular case is reported rather than silently returning zero. Because the criterion is purely deterministic and depends on no observed response, the sealed-spec model fits it exactly, and repeat count above one under a constant seed would be correctly flagged as degenerate by construction.
REDUCTION: NONE for the criterion itself, with a precise reason. A design over a discretised region can indeed be written as an indicator bitstring, one bit per candidate support point, which is how exchange algorithms are commonly coded, so the ENCODING reduces cleanly. What does not reduce is the SCORE. evaluate_bitstring returns the fraction of positions matching a hash-derived target, which is a fixed additive function of the bits; D-efficiency is a determinant of a matrix built from the selected points, which is irreducibly non-additive because it is precisely a measure of how far the chosen points are from being collinear. No choice of seed or length makes an additive function equal a determinant, and the seed cannot be steered because the target is a hash. The nearest useful thing is not a bitstring caricature but the thirty-line executor named above. WHAT DOES SURVIVE, and it is worth running: the bench can supply the NULL for a design search. Run a producer-side exchange search over indicator bitstrings on the matching-fraction landscape at the same budget the real exchange algorithm would use, and record the best-of-n distribution. That is the correct null for the claim that an exchange algorithm exploited structure rather than merely sampling a lot, and because the bench landscape is additive and single-peaked it gives the strongest possible version of that null, in the sense that any search doing worse than it is doing worse than a search on a landscape with no interaction terms at all. WHICH CLAIM: the surviving fragment supports only a statement about the search procedure's budget efficiency, never about optimality of any design.

QUESTION: Does a particular sequence of machine instructions, run on a small virtual computer, actually compute a specified logic function of its inputs?
MECHANISM: An Avidian is a circular sequence of instructions executed by a virtual CPU with a handful of registers, two stacks, and instruction pointers called heads. Some instructions do arithmetic and bit operations; others move heads, allocate memory and divide; a set of no-operation instructions act as modifiers that change which register the preceding instruction touches, which is what makes the language robust to point mutation. Input instructions pull numbers from the environment and output instructions push a result back. The environment watches the outputs, and when an output equals a designated logic function of recent inputs, such as NOT of one input or the EQUALS of two, it credits the organism with a merit multiplier, which buys more CPU cycles per update, which lets it replicate faster. That is the entire coupling between computation and fitness. In the 2003 experiment the point was that EQU, which needs five NAND operations to build, only ever appeared in populations where the simpler intermediate functions were also rewarded: the stepping stones were required.
CANDIDATE: The instruction sequence, the genome. What is judged is the outputs it emits given the inputs the environment supplies.
WORLD: A grid of cells with a resource and reward schedule. The environment supplies the input numbers, the list of which logic functions are rewarded and by how much, and the CPU cycles that reward buys. The reward schedule is the environment's entire content, and changing it changes what evolves.
WHAT_CHANGES: The genome sequence and which logic function the environment rewards.
MEASURED: For the single-genotype question, whether the target function was performed, and on how many input cases it was performed correctly. The natural continuous version is the fraction of input pairs answered correctly, between zero and one.
INFORMATIVE_FAILURE: Moderately informative and easy to over-read. A genome that fails to emit the target function tells you the sequence lacks a required primitive, or that the heads never reach the output instruction. That is a debugging fact. The genuinely informative failure lives at the population level and this template cannot reach it: the finding that matters is that EQU never appears when the intermediate rewards are switched off, and that is a failure of a POPULATION under a reward schedule, not of a genotype. A single-genotype failure leaves behind almost nothing about evolvability.
SOURCE_CHECK: VERIFIED - Lenski, Ofria, Pennock and Adami, The Evolutionary Origin of Complex Features, Nature 2003, is the correct reference and it is the EQU experiment with the stepping-stone reward schedule. The two named environmental resources, logic NOT and logic EQU, correspond to the simplest and the hardest of the rewarded functions in that work.
BLOCKER: R-NOW - for the degraded truth-table version below nothing is missing; the constraint is INTERPRETIVE, in that the hidden target is a random Boolean function rather than a named one, so the result is about arbitrary functions and not about EQU. R-COMPOSE - to compare genotypes the producer must run many specs, because no search is allowed inside one. CONTROL FLOW. R-BACKEND - Avida is real, runnable and open, and invoking it and fossilizing one scalar needs no new bench internals. MEASUREMENT. R-EXECUTOR - a small stack-machine kind that runs a supplied opcode sequence over all input pairs and returns the fraction correct. MEASUREMENT.
FAITHFUL: A faithful version needs an instruction-set interpreter with registers and heads, an environment object holding a reward schedule, and the ability to run one genome against many input cases and aggregate. For the result that made the paper matter it additionally needs a population, mutation, and differential replication rate, none of which the bench has.
REDUCTION: There is a reduction that runs TODAY with no new code, and it is better than it first looks. Read a bitstring of length two to the power k as the complete truth table of a k-input Boolean function. evaluate_bitstring already returns the fraction of positions matching a hidden target, so it is already computing the agreement of your candidate function with a hidden Boolean function over all inputs. Set length to 16, so k is 4, and submit one fixed truth table. Now set repeat.seed_derivation = sha256_index with a high count: each repeat scores the SAME candidate function against a DIFFERENT random target function. What comes out is the null distribution of agreement between an arbitrary function and a random one, measured rather than assumed. That is exactly the baseline any claim of the form this genome computes something must be compared against, and it is currently missing from every such claim on this bench. Note the seed-derivation subtlety explicitly: under constant the same spec is degenerate_by_construction, one target, one candidate, zero variance. Beyond that, an R-EXECUTOR step that is still small: a stack machine with eight opcodes, NAND among them, that executes a supplied sequence over all two to the k input assignments and returns the fraction of cases matching a NAMED function such as EQU. Naming the target is the one thing the bitstring version cannot do, and it is the difference between measuring an arbitrary function and measuring the one the literature cares about. WHAT IT PRESERVES: execution of a supplied program as the source of the measurement, a continuous correctness scale, and the honest scope of the template's own rationale, that mechanical production of an output is not an evolutionary claim. WHAT IT LOSES: the merit economy, replication, the population, mutation, and therefore the stepping-stone result that is the entire scientific content of the cited paper. This must be stated on any fossil produced or the result will be mis-cited. WHICH CLAIM IT SUPPORTS: a null-calibration claim, what agreement looks like by chance, and later a mechanical-correctness claim about one supplied program. Nothing whatever about evolvability.

QUESTION: Given a candidate bridging term that connects two unrelated bodies of literature, can a statistical model predict from a few cheap features whether that bridge is a real, relevant connection rather than noise?
MECHANISM: In an Arrowsmith style two node search, two literatures are retrieved and the terms they share are extracted. There are typically hundreds or thousands of them and almost all are worthless, so the practical problem is ranking. Torvik and Smalheiser computed, for each shared term, a set of cheap features, how often it appears in each literature, how many distinct literatures it occurs in, its indexing category, how cohesive its usage is, and fitted a logistic regression of those features against expert relevance judgements. The fitted model returns a probability of relevance, the terms are sorted by it, and a human curator reads only the top of the list. The method is ordinary supervised ranking; what makes it a discovery method is what the features are computed over.
CANDIDATE: One shared bridging term, represented as a feature vector, judged by its predicted relevance.
WORLD: A bibliographic corpus, a chosen pair of literatures, and a gold set of expert relevance judgements. The environment supplies both the feature values and the labels, and the labels are the expensive part.
WHAT_CHANGES: The feature vector, the number of features, and, in the template as written, the world seed which determines the hidden target the bits are compared against.
MEASURED: In the real method, a predicted probability in 0 to 1, evaluated in aggregate by area under the curve or precision at k. In the template, evaluate_bitstring's score, which is the fraction of bits agreeing with a hash derived target.
INFORMATIVE_FAILURE: This has to be answered bluntly, because the template does not implement the method. It replaces a regression fitted against labelled data with agreement against a hash derived random vector, so a FALSIFIED verdict says only that a fixed eight bit pattern happened to disagree with a hash. It leaves nothing about bridging terms. What it does leave, if run with many repeats under sha256_index, is the null distribution of agreement between a fixed pattern and independent random targets, which is a useful bench calibration and has no connection to discovery informatics. There is a second, sharper thing a failure would expose here, and it is a defect in the template as written. The three bits choices, 11110000, 10101010 and 11111111, all have identical score distributions against a uniformly random target, namely a binomial with eight trials and probability one half divided by eight. Two of them have four ones and one has eight, and it makes no difference, because the score depends only on Hamming distance to an unknown uniform target and every fixed pattern is exchangeable under that. The three arms are therefore not separable, and the bits axis is vacuous as long as the target is a fresh hash. That is a real finding about the template and it should be recorded before anything is run.
SOURCE_CHECK: VERIFIED. Torvik and Smalheiser, A quantitative model for linking two disparate sets of articles in MEDLINE, Bioinformatics, 2007. The paper addresses exactly the problem of ranking the many shared terms produced by the Arrowsmith two node search by fitting a model over computable term features, and the logistic characterisation in the template matches. Attribution and method both check out.
BLOCKER: R-REPAIR: a missing parameter, and then a validity problem that repair does not fix. The length axis is null while every bits choice is eight characters long, so length must be set to 8 or the spec is inconsistent. Once repaired the spec runs, but it measures bit agreement with a hash, not relevance, so R-REPAIR buys execution and not validity. R-EXECUTOR: a measurement capability. Nothing in the bench applies a coefficient vector to a feature vector and returns a probability. R-BACKEND: an adjudication capability. The labels live entirely outside the bench. There is no way for a spec to be handed a gold standard, so a labelled term set and a fitted model have to be orchestrated externally and fossilized. R-COMPOSE: an adjudication capability. Ranking quality is a property of a list, not of one item, so area under the curve or precision at k cannot be a single spec's outcome.
FAITHFUL: A faithful version needs a labelled set of bridging terms with the published feature definitions, a model with fixed coefficients, and a held out split, and it would report area under the curve or precision at k. The sealed spec with one scalar comparison can carry that final number. What it cannot carry is the fitting step, because fitting is search over parameters and search inside a spec is forbidden, so the model must be fitted upstream and the spec may only evaluate it. That separation is actually good discipline and would improve the original method's reporting.
REDUCTION: Two reductions, and the first one is available now. First, invert the reading of the hidden target. Fix length at 8 and treat the hash derived target as the unknown rule rather than as noise. Hold seed_root fixed with constant derivation and count one, since more repeats would be flagged degenerate_by_construction, and emit one spec per candidate hypothesis vector. Across the 256 possible eight bit hypotheses, which is R-COMPOSE over 256 cheap specs, the whole score landscape is recovered and the hidden rule is identified exactly.
